    // A file and a trainer must agree on normalising: inputs scaled one way and read the
    // other are exactly the silent mismatch the shape check exists to prevent.
    if (has_normaliser != self.options.normalize) {
        return error.WeightsShape;
    }
    const normaliser: usize = if (has_normaliser) 2 * self.n_obs else 0;
    if (bytes.len != @sizeOf(Header) + (3 * count + normaliser) * @sizeOf(f32)) {
        return error.NotAWeightsFile;
    }
    // Copied into aligned floats: the bytes came from a file and owe nothing to alignment.
    const values: []f32 = try self.gpa.alloc(f32, 3 * count);
    defer self.gpa.free(values);
    @memcpy(sliceAsBytes(values), bytes[@sizeOf(Header)..][0 .. 3 * count * @sizeOf(f32)]);
    self.ppo.pipe.upload(.params, values[0..count]);
    self.ppo.pipe.upload(.adam_m, values[count .. 2 * count]);
    self.ppo.pipe.upload(.adam_v, values[2 * count .. 3 * count]);
    @memcpy(self.ppo.cpu_params, values[0..count]);
    self.ppo.adam_step = header.adam_step;
    self.decisions = header.decisions;
    self.steps = header.steps;
    self.iterations = header.iterations;
    if (has_normaliser) {
        const extra: []f32 = try self.gpa.alloc(f32, normaliser);
        defer self.gpa.free(extra);
        const start: usize = @sizeOf(Header) + 3 * count * @sizeOf(f32);
        @memcpy(sliceAsBytes(extra), bytes[start..]);
        // The file keeps each input's mean and variance; the normaliser keeps the sum of squared deviations,
        // the variance times the count.
        self.observation_normalizer.count = @floatFromInt(header.observations_seen);
        const n: f64 = @max(self.observation_normalizer.count, 1);
        const means: []const f32 = extra[0..self.n_obs];
        const variances: []const f32 = extra[self.n_obs..];
        const own_means: []f64 = self.observation_normalizer.mean;
        const own_sums: []f64 = self.observation_normalizer.m2;
        for (own_means, own_sums, means, variances) |*mean, *m2, saved_mean, saved_var| {
            mean.* = saved_mean;
            m2.* = @as(f64, saved_var) * n;
        }
    }
    // A batch half-collected under the old weights would be judged against the new ones.
    self.cursor = 0;
    self.batch = .{};
    // The helping hand where the schedule has it after the batches these weights trained, not where a
    // fresh trainer starts it.
    self.env.fleet.options.task.gains.assist = self.assistAfter(self.iterations);
}

A long run has to survive being stopped, so it runs in chunks: each loads the checkpoint, learns for a few minutes, and saves — weights and the optimiser's moments both, because an optimiser resumed without its moments takes full-size steps in directions it had already learned to damp.

Trainer.save
/// The weights to a file, for runs on a machine with a disk. Written to a temporary name
/// and renamed into place, so a run killed mid-write keeps its previous file intact.
pub fn save(self: *Self, io: Io, path: []const u8) !void {
    const bytes: []u8 = try self.exportWeights(self.gpa);
    defer self.gpa.free(bytes);
    if (std.fs.path.dirname(path)) |dir| {
        try Io.Dir.cwd().createDirPath(io, dir);
    }
    var temp_buffer: [512]u8 = undefined;
    const temp: []const u8 = try bufPrint(&temp_buffer, "{s}.partial", .{path});
    {
        const file: Io.File = try Io.Dir.cwd().createFile(io, temp, .{});
        defer file.close(io);
        try file.writeStreamingAll(io, bytes);
    }
    try Io.Dir.cwd().rename(temp, Io.Dir.cwd(), path, io);
}

The clip it learns from is five seconds of getting up off the floor: the capture's hips go from six centimetres to eighty-one across it, so every episode starts somewhere between lying down and standing. Clips carve out such a stretch with window.

Clip.window
/// A stretch of this clip, `count` frames from `first`, as a clip of its own.
///
/// Learning a skill usually wants only the part of a capture where the skill happens - five
/// seconds of getting up, not the fall before it and the standing after - and a clip that
/// starts where the interesting part starts makes reference-state starts land in it too.
pub fn window(self: *const Clip, first: usize, count: usize) !Clip {
    assertf(count > 1 and first + count <= self.frame_count, @src(), "frames {d}..{d} of {d}", .{
        first,
        first + count,
        self.frame_count,
    });
    const targets: []f32 = try self.gpa.dupe(f32, self.targets[first * self.nq ..][0 .. count * self.nq]);
    errdefer self.gpa.free(targets);
    const residual: []f32 = try self.gpa.dupe(f32, self.residual[first..][0..count]);
    errdefer self.gpa.free(residual);
    const residual_body: []u32 = try self.gpa.dupe(u32, self.residual_body[first..][0..count]);
    return .{
        .gpa = self.gpa,
        .frame_count = count,
        .frame_time = self.frame_time,
        .nq = self.nq,
        .targets = targets,
        .residual = residual,
        .residual_body = residual_body,
    };
}

The trainer. PPO itself - the clipped objective, GAE's advantages - is explained in zimrrl (zimrrl 6.1, 6.2); PpoTrainer is its implementation here, with a Gaussian policy: a network for the mean, a learned log standard deviation per action. Two choices matter in practice for tracking. The exploration noise starts small (initial_log_std), close to holding the reference pose, because a wide start falls immediately and never learns to stand. And the update runs one minibatch at a time (updateSlice), because a minibatch is what a frame can afford.

Layer
/// A dense layer's weights and biases, as graph parameters and as the tensors that hold them.
pub const Layer = struct {
    w: zn.Tensor(f32),
    b: zn.Tensor(f32),
    w_var: zn.Var = undefined,
    b_var: zn.Var = undefined,

    pub fn init(
        arena: Allocator,
        random: Random,
        in: usize,
        out: usize,
        gain: f32,
    ) !Layer {
        const w: zn.Tensor(f32) = try .alloc(arena, &.{ in, out });
        const b: zn.Tensor(f32) = try .alloc(arena, &.{ 1, out });
        const limit: f32 = gain * @sqrt(6.0 / float(in + out));
        for (w.data) |*x| {
            x.* = limit * (2.0 * random.float(f32) - 1.0);
        }
        @memset(b.data, 0.0);
        return .{ .w = w, .b = b };
    }

    /// x W + 1 b on the graph (the bias through a ones column: `add` needs equal shapes).
    pub fn apply(
        self: *Layer,
        graph: *zn.Graph(f32),
        x: zn.Var,
        ones: zn.Var,
    ) !zn.Var {
        self.w_var = try graph.parameter(self.w);
        self.b_var = try graph.parameter(self.b);
        return graph.add(try graph.matmul(x, self.w_var), try graph.matmul(ones, self.b_var));
    }

    /// The same, for ONE row, in plain loops - collection must not build a graph per step.
    pub fn forward(
        self: *const Layer,
        x: []const f32,
        out: []f32,
        squash: bool,
    ) void {
        const n_out: usize = self.w.shape[1];
        for (0..n_out) |j| {
            var sum: f32 = self.b.data[j];
            for (x, 0..) |xi, i| {
                sum += xi * self.w.data[i * n_out + j];
            }
            out[j] = if (squash) tanh(sum) else sum;
        }
    }
};
TrainerOptions
pub const TrainerOptions = struct {
    hidden: usize = 64,
    /// Environment steps per PPO iteration.
    horizon: usize = 2048,
    minibatch: usize = 256,
    epochs: usize = 5,
    /// ** ADAM's rate. `ppoUpdate` steps plain SGD; the trainer runs the minibatch itself and
    /// steps Adam (`updateSlice`), because no single SGD rate suits every parameter of the
    /// policy: a small one does not move it, and a large one drives its mean into the action clamp
    /// within a few iterations - a star pose, every joint at its offset limit.
    learning_rate: f64 = 3.0e-4,
    /// Rewards are scaled by this before they reach the rollout, so value targets stay near
    /// unit size: 5 per step alive makes returns of ~130, and plain SGD on a squared error that
    /// large diverges. The printed returns are unscaled.
    reward_scale: f32 = 0.05,
    /// * Start NEAR THE STATUE: sigma = e^-1.5 = 0.22, times the 0.5 rad action scale. A wider
    /// start flails every joint by tenths of a radian, falls sooner than holding the reference pose
    /// would, and PPO does not climb back from there.
    initial_log_std: f32 = -1.5,
    seed: u64 = 20260919,
};
TrainerStats
/// One finished PPO iteration.
pub const TrainerStats = struct {
    iteration: usize = 0,
    samples: usize = 0,
    episodes: u32 = 0,
    mean_length: f32 = 0,
    mean_return: f32 = 0,
};
PpoTrainer
/// PPO on a `HumanoidEnv`, in slices a frame can afford: `collect` runs environment steps into
/// the rollout, `updateEpoch` runs ONE epoch of the update (call it until it returns true).
/// zimrnum's `ppoUpdate`, `gae` and `RolloutBuffer` underneath; a 64-64 tanh Gaussian policy and
/// value net built on its graph; observations normalised by running statistics.
pub const PpoTrainer = struct {
    arena_state: ArenaAllocator,
    gpa: Allocator,
    env: *HumanoidEnv,
    options: TrainerOptions,
    p1: Layer,
    p2: Layer,
    p3: Layer,
    v1: Layer,
    v2: Layer,
    v3: Layer,
    log_std: zn.Tensor(f32),
    graph: zn.Graph(f32),
    model: zrl.PpoModel(f32),
    norm: Normalizer,
    raw: []f32,
    normed: []f32,
    a1: []f32,
    a2: []f32,
    mu: []f32,
    act: []f32,
    val: []f32,
    observations: zn.Tensor(f32),
    actions: zn.Tensor(f32),
    advantages: []f64,
    returns: []f64,
    rollout: zrl.RolloutBuffer,
    rng: Random.DefaultPrng,
    episode_seed: u64,
    episode_length: u32 = 0,
    episode_return: f32 = 0,
    finished: u32 = 0,
    finished_length: u64 = 0,
    finished_return: f64 = 0,
    /// 0 while collecting; the number of update epochs done while updating.
    epoch: usize = 0,
    /// The next minibatch of the current epoch (`updateSlice`).
    minibatch_index: usize = 0,
    /// Adam's first and second moments, one pair per weight tensor, and its step count.
    moments: []zn.Tensor(f32),
    velocities: []zn.Tensor(f32),
    adam_step: usize = 0,
    iteration: usize = 0,
    last: TrainerStats = .{},

    pub fn init(
        gpa: Allocator,
        env: *HumanoidEnv,
        options: TrainerOptions,
    ) !*PpoTrainer {
        const t: *PpoTrainer = try gpa.create(PpoTrainer);
        errdefer gpa.destroy(t);
        // whole-init-first: the whole struct first - defaults applied, every field named.
        t.* = .{
            .arena_state = undefined,
            .gpa = undefined,
            .env = undefined,
            .options = undefined,
            .p1 = undefined,
            .p2 = undefined,
            .p3 = undefined,
            .v1 = undefined,
            .v2 = undefined,
            .v3 = undefined,
            .log_std = undefined,
            .graph = undefined,
            .model = undefined,
            .norm = undefined,
            .raw = undefined,
            .normed = undefined,
            .a1 = undefined,
            .a2 = undefined,
            .mu = undefined,
            .act = undefined,
            .val = undefined,
            .observations = undefined,
            .actions = undefined,
            .advantages = undefined,
            .returns = undefined,
            .rollout = undefined,
            .rng = undefined,
            .episode_seed = undefined,
            .moments = undefined,
            .velocities = undefined,
        };
        t.arena_state = ArenaAllocator.init(gpa);
        errdefer t.arena_state.deinit();
        const arena: Allocator = t.arena_state.allocator();
        t.gpa = gpa;
        t.env = env;
        t.options = options;
        t.episode_length = 0;
        t.episode_return = 0;
        t.finished = 0;
        t.finished_length = 0;
        t.finished_return = 0;
        t.epoch = 0;
        t.minibatch_index = 0;
        t.iteration = 0;
        t.last = .{};
        assertf(options.horizon % options.minibatch == 0, @src(), "the horizon must be whole minibatches", .{});
        const n_obs: usize = env.observationSize();
        const n_act: usize = env.actionSize();
        const hidden: usize = options.hidden;
        const batch: usize = options.minibatch;
        t.rng = Random.DefaultPrng.init(options.seed);
        const random: Random = t.rng.random();
        t.p1 = try Layer.init(arena, random, n_obs, hidden, 1.0);
        t.p2 = try Layer.init(arena, random, hidden, hidden, 1.0);
        t.p3 = try Layer.init(arena, random, hidden, n_act, 0.01);
        t.v1 = try Layer.init(arena, random, n_obs, hidden, 1.0);
        t.v2 = try Layer.init(arena, random, hidden, hidden, 1.0);
        t.v3 = try Layer.init(arena, random, hidden, 1, 1.0);
        t.log_std = try zn.Tensor(f32).alloc(arena, &.{ 1, n_act });
        @memset(t.log_std.data, options.initial_log_std);

        // -- The update's graph, built once at minibatch size. --
        t.graph = zn.Graph(f32).init(arena);
        // The graph lives as long as the trainer and runs thousands of passes: its backward
        // temporaries need an allocator that can free (zimrnum's `Graph.scratch`).
        t.graph.useScratchAllocator(gpa);
        const g: *zn.Graph(f32) = &t.graph;
        const obs_leaf: zn.Tensor(f32) = try .alloc(arena, &.{ batch, n_obs });
        const act_leaf: zn.Tensor(f32) = try .alloc(arena, &.{ batch, n_act });
        const adv_leaf: zn.Tensor(f32) = try .alloc(arena, &.{ batch, 1 });
        const old_leaf: zn.Tensor(f32) = try .alloc(arena, &.{ batch, 1 });
        const ret_leaf: zn.Tensor(f32) = try .alloc(arena, &.{ batch, 1 });
        const ones_t: zn.Tensor(f32) = try .alloc(arena, &.{ batch, 1 });
        for ([_]zn.Tensor(f32){ obs_leaf, act_leaf, adv_leaf, old_leaf, ret_leaf }) |leaf| {
            @memset(leaf.data, 0.0);
        }
        @memset(ones_t.data, 1.0);
        const obs_var: zn.Var = try g.constant(obs_leaf);
        const act_var: zn.Var = try g.constant(act_leaf);
        const adv_var: zn.Var = try g.constant(adv_leaf);
        const old_var: zn.Var = try g.constant(old_leaf);
        const ret_var: zn.Var = try g.constant(ret_leaf);
        const ones: zn.Var = try g.constant(ones_t);
        const h1: zn.Var = try g.tanh(try t.p1.apply(g, obs_var, ones));
        const h2: zn.Var = try g.tanh(try t.p2.apply(g, h1, ones));
        const mean: zn.Var = try t.p3.apply(g, h2, ones);
        const log_std_var: zn.Var = try g.parameter(t.log_std);
        const log_prob_new: zn.Var = try g.diagGaussianLogProb(mean, log_std_var, act_leaf);
        const clip_loss: zrl.PpoClipLoss(f32) = try .build(g, log_prob_new, old_leaf.data, adv_leaf.data, 0.2);
        const k1: zn.Var = try g.tanh(try t.v1.apply(g, obs_var, ones));
        const k2: zn.Var = try g.tanh(try t.v2.apply(g, k1, ones));
        const value: zn.Var = try t.v3.apply(g, k2, ones);
        const value_loss: zn.Var = try g.mseLoss(value, ret_var);
        const loss: zn.Var = try g.add(clip_loss.loss, try g.scale(value_loss, 0.5));
        const weights: []zn.Tensor(f32) = try arena.dupe(zn.Tensor(f32), &.{
            t.p1.w, t.p1.b, t.p2.w, t.p2.b, t.p3.w, t.p3.b, t.log_std,
            t.v1.w, t.v1.b, t.v2.w, t.v2.b, t.v3.w, t.v3.b,
        });
        const parameters: []zn.Var = try arena.dupe(zn.Var, &.{
            t.p1.w_var, t.p1.b_var, t.p2.w_var, t.p2.b_var, t.p3.w_var, t.p3.b_var, log_std_var,
            t.v1.w_var, t.v1.b_var, t.v2.w_var, t.v2.b_var, t.v3.w_var, t.v3.b_var,
        });
        t.moments = try arena.alloc(zn.Tensor(f32), weights.len);
        t.velocities = try arena.alloc(zn.Tensor(f32), weights.len);
        for (weights, t.moments, t.velocities) |w, *mo, *ve| {
            mo.* = try zn.Tensor(f32).alloc(arena, w.shape[0..w.rank]);
            ve.* = try zn.Tensor(f32).alloc(arena, w.shape[0..w.rank]);
            @memset(mo.data, 0.0);
            @memset(ve.data, 0.0);
        }
        t.adam_step = 0;
        t.model = .{
            .graph = g,
            .observations = obs_var,
            .actions = act_var,
            .advantages = adv_var,
            .log_prob_old = old_var,
            .returns = ret_var,
            .loss = loss,
            .clip_loss = clip_loss,
            .log_prob_new = log_prob_new,
            .weights = weights,
            .parameters = parameters,
        };

        // -- Collection buffers. --
        t.norm = .{ .mean = try arena.alloc(f64, n_obs), .m2 = try arena.alloc(f64, n_obs) };
        @memset(t.norm.mean, 0.0);
        @memset(t.norm.m2, 0.0);
        t.raw = try arena.alloc(f32, n_obs);
        t.normed = try arena.alloc(f32, n_obs);
        t.a1 = try arena.alloc(f32, hidden);
        t.a2 = try arena.alloc(f32, hidden);
        t.mu = try arena.alloc(f32, n_act);
        t.act = try arena.alloc(f32, n_act);
        t.val = try arena.alloc(f32, 1);
        t.observations = try zn.Tensor(f32).alloc(arena, &.{ options.horizon, n_obs });
        t.actions = try zn.Tensor(f32).alloc(arena, &.{ options.horizon, n_act });
        t.advantages = try arena.alloc(f64, options.horizon);
        t.returns = try arena.alloc(f64, options.horizon);
        t.rollout = try zrl.RolloutBuffer.init(arena, options.horizon);
        t.episode_seed = options.seed;
        try env.reset(t.episode_seed, t.raw);
        return t;
    }

    pub fn deinit(t: *PpoTrainer) void {
        t.graph.deinitScratch();
        t.arena_state.deinit();
        t.gpa.destroy(t);
    }

    pub fn rolloutFull(t: *const PpoTrainer) bool {
        return t.rollout.len == t.options.horizon;
    }

    fn valueOf(t: *PpoTrainer, x: []const f32) f32 {
        t.v1.forward(x, t.a1, true);
        t.v2.forward(t.a1, t.a2, true);
        t.v3.forward(t.a2, t.val, false);
        return t.val[0];
    }

    /// Run up to `max_steps` environment steps into the rollout; stops when it is full.
    pub fn collect(t: *PpoTrainer, max_steps: usize) !usize {
        const n_obs: usize = t.raw.len;
        const n_act: usize = t.act.len;
        var ran: usize = 0;
        while (ran < max_steps and !t.rolloutFull()) : (ran += 1) {
            const row: usize = t.rollout.len;
            t.norm.update(t.raw);
            t.norm.apply(t.raw, t.normed);
            @memcpy(t.observations.data[row * n_obs ..][0..n_obs], t.normed);
            t.p1.forward(t.normed, t.a1, true);
            t.p2.forward(t.a1, t.a2, true);
            t.p3.forward(t.a2, t.mu, false);
            var log_prob: f64 = 0.0;
            for (0..n_act) |k| {
                const noise: f32 = t.rng.random().floatNorm(f32);
                t.act[k] = t.mu[k] + @exp(t.log_std.data[k]) * noise;
                log_prob += -0.5 * @as(f64, noise * noise) - @as(f64, t.log_std.data[k]) - 0.5 * @log(2.0 * pi);
            }
            @memcpy(t.actions.data[row * n_act ..][0..n_act], t.act);
            const v_now: f32 = t.valueOf(t.normed);
            const result: StepResult = try t.env.step(t.act, t.raw);
            t.episode_length += 1;
            t.episode_return += result.reward;
            var v_next: f32 = 0.0;
            if (!result.terminated) {
                t.norm.apply(t.raw, t.normed);
                v_next = t.valueOf(t.normed);
            }
            const scaled: f32 = t.options.reward_scale * result.reward;
            try t.rollout.record(scaled, v_now, v_next, result.terminated, result.truncated, log_prob);
            if (result.terminated or result.truncated) {
                t.finished += 1;
                t.finished_length += t.episode_length;
                t.finished_return += t.episode_return;
                t.episode_length = 0;
                t.episode_return = 0.0;
                t.episode_seed += 1;
                try t.env.reset(t.episode_seed, t.raw);
            }
        }
        return ran;
    }

    /// The current policy's MEAN action for a raw observation - no exploration noise: what the
    /// policy has learned, for watching. Uses the trainer's normaliser without updating it.
    pub fn policyMean(
        t: *PpoTrainer,
        observation: []const f32,
        action: []f32,
    ) void {
        t.norm.apply(observation, t.normed);
        t.p1.forward(t.normed, t.a1, true);
        t.p2.forward(t.a1, t.a2, true);
        t.p3.forward(t.a2, action, false);
    }

    /// Shuffle the rollout's rows - observations, actions, advantages, returns and the steps
    /// with their log-probs, together - so consecutive chunks are random minibatches.
    fn shuffleRollout(t: *PpoTrainer) void {
        const n_obs: usize = t.raw.len;
        const n_act: usize = t.act.len;
        const random: Random = t.rng.random();
        var i: usize = t.rollout.len;
        while (i > 1) {
            i -= 1;
            const j: usize = random.uintLessThan(usize, i + 1);
            if (i == j) {
                continue;
            }
            for (0..n_obs) |k| {
                swap(f32, &t.observations.data[i * n_obs + k], &t.observations.data[j * n_obs + k]);
            }
            for (0..n_act) |k| {
                swap(f32, &t.actions.data[i * n_act + k], &t.actions.data[j * n_act + k]);
            }
            swap(f64, &t.advantages[i], &t.advantages[j]);
            swap(f64, &t.returns[i], &t.returns[j]);
            swap(zrl.RolloutStep, &t.rollout.steps[i], &t.rollout.steps[j]);
            swap(f64, &t.rollout.log_prob[i], &t.rollout.log_prob[j]);
        }
    }

    /// ONE MINIBATCH of the PPO update - the unit a 30 fps frame can afford (a whole epoch is
    /// many frames' worth on a phone). Advantages are computed and normalised over the whole rollout
    /// once, the rows shuffled at the start of every epoch, and `ppoUpdate` handed one
    /// minibatch-sized chunk. Returns true when the whole update is done: the rollout is then
    /// empty for the next iteration and `last` holds its numbers.
    pub fn updateSlice(t: *PpoTrainer) !bool {
        assertf(t.rolloutFull(), @src(), "updateSlice before the rollout is full", .{});
        if (t.epoch == 0 and t.minibatch_index == 0) {
            try zrl.gae(t.rollout.steps[0..t.rollout.len], 0.99, 0.95, t.advantages, t.returns);
            try zrl.normalizeAdvantages(f64, t.advantages, 1.0e-8);
        }
        if (t.minibatch_index == 0) {
            t.shuffleRollout();
        }
        const size: usize = t.options.minibatch;
        const at: usize = t.minibatch_index * size;
        // ** The minibatch by hand, so it can step ADAM (`ppoUpdate` steps plain SGD): the
        // chunk's rows into the graph's leaves (contiguous after the shuffle), the clip node's
        // copies refreshed, the loss and gradients recomputed, then one Adam step per tensor.
        const n_obs: usize = t.raw.len;
        const n_act: usize = t.act.len;
        const g: *zn.Graph(f32) = &t.graph;
        @memcpy(g.valueOf(t.model.observations).data, t.observations.data[at * n_obs ..][0 .. size * n_obs]);
        @memcpy(g.valueOf(t.model.actions).data, t.actions.data[at * n_act ..][0 .. size * n_act]);
        const adv_leaf: []f32 = g.valueOf(t.model.advantages).data;
        const old_leaf: []f32 = g.valueOf(t.model.log_prob_old).data;
        const ret_leaf: []f32 = g.valueOf(t.model.returns).data;
        for (0..size) |i| {
            adv_leaf[i] = @floatCast(t.advantages[at + i]);
            old_leaf[i] = @floatCast(t.rollout.log_prob[at + i]);
            ret_leaf[i] = @floatCast(t.returns[at + i]);
        }
        try t.model.clip_loss.setInputs(old_leaf, adv_leaf);
        try g.recompute();
        try g.backward(t.model.loss);
        t.adam_step += 1;
        const hyper: zn.Adam = .{ .rate = t.options.learning_rate };
        for (t.model.weights, t.model.parameters, t.moments, t.velocities) |w, v, mo, ve| {
            try zn.adamStep(f32, w, w, try g.gradOf(v), mo, ve, hyper, t.adam_step);
        }
        t.minibatch_index += 1;
        if (t.minibatch_index * size < t.options.horizon) {
            return false;
        }
        t.minibatch_index = 0;
        t.epoch += 1;
        if (t.epoch < t.options.epochs) {
            return false;
        }
        t.epoch = 0;
        t.iteration += 1;
        const episodes: f32 = float(t.finished);
        const mean_length: f32 = if (t.finished > 0) float(t.finished_length) / episodes else float(t.options.horizon);
        t.last = .{
            .iteration = t.iteration,
            .samples = t.iteration * t.options.horizon,
            .episodes = t.finished,
            .mean_length = mean_length,
            .mean_return = if (t.finished > 0) @floatCast(t.finished_return / float(t.finished)) else 0.0,
        };
        t.finished = 0;
        t.finished_length = 0;
        t.finished_return = 0.0;
        t.rollout.len = 0;
        return true;
    }

    /// One whole epoch of the update (`updateSlice` until the epoch turns). Returns true when
    /// the whole update is done.
    pub fn updateEpoch(t: *PpoTrainer) !bool {
        while (true) {
            if (try t.updateSlice()) {
                return true;
            }
            if (t.minibatch_index == 0) {
                return false;
            }
        }
    }
};

10.5 A simpler gym: standing and walking forward#

HumanoidEnv wraps a humanoid, a floor and the physics into the loop reinforcement learning expects: reset starts an episode and writes the first observation; step applies an action, advances the physics, and returns a reward and whether the episode ended. An action does not command torques directly. It offsets the pose the joints are servoed toward, scaled by action_scale, and a stable PD servo at spring_hz turns that into torques — so a zero action means "hold the reference pose", and the policy learns corrections. The reward pays for staying up and moving forward, and charges for effort; an episode ends when the torso falls below healthy_height, or at max_steps.

Options
pub const Options = struct {
    /// Physics steps per policy step: 2 makes a 30 Hz policy over 60 Hz physics.
    substeps: u32 = 2,
    physics_hz: f32 = 60.0,
    /// The largest joint offset an action of 1 asks for, in radians.
    action_scale: f32 = 0.5,
    /// The low-level spring's natural frequency: `Tracker` reaches a target in ~1/f.
    spring_hz: f32 = 20.0,
    /// Gymnasium Humanoid's reward shape.
    forward_weight: f32 = 1.25,
    healthy_reward: f32 = 5.0,
    control_weight: f32 = 0.1,
    /// A fall: the torso's origin under this height, in metres (it stands at ~1.28).
    healthy_height: f32 = 0.9,
    /// Episode length in POLICY steps; 500 at 30 Hz is 16.7 s.
    max_steps: u32 = 500,
    /// Uniform noise on the joints' starting angles and speeds, as Gymnasium's reset noise.
    reset_noise: f32 = 0.01,
};
StepResult
pub const StepResult = struct {
    reward: f32,
    /// The episode ended in a fall.
    terminated: bool,
    /// The episode ran out of time.
    truncated: bool,
};
HumanoidEnv
pub const HumanoidEnv = struct {
    gpa: Allocator,
    options: Options,
    doc: codecs.xml.Document,
    robot: mjcf.Robot,
    imported: robot_mjcf.Imported,
    data: rbt.Data,
    world: zimrphysics.World,
    bridge: robot_physics.Bridge,
    tracker: dance.Tracker,
    /// Joint coordinates of the base pose (standing, feet on the floor), and the current target.
    base: []f32,
    target: []f32,
    previous_action: []f32,
    /// qpos / dof addresses of the actuated hinges, in joint order.
    hinge_qpos: []u32,
    hinge_dof: []u32,
    a_des: []f32,
    torque: []f32,
    full: []f32,
    dense: []f32,
    rng: Random.DefaultPrng,
    steps: u32,

    /// Build the environment from MJCF text (a floating humanoid made of hinges). Call `reset`
    /// before the first `step`.
    pub fn init(
        gpa: Allocator,
        xml: []const u8,
        options: Options,
    ) !*HumanoidEnv {
        const env: *HumanoidEnv = try gpa.create(HumanoidEnv);
        errdefer gpa.destroy(env);
        // whole-init-first: the whole struct first - defaults applied, every field named.
        env.* = .{
            .gpa = undefined,
            .options = undefined,
            .doc = undefined,
            .robot = undefined,
            .imported = undefined,
            .data = undefined,
            .world = undefined,
            .bridge = undefined,
            .tracker = undefined,
            .base = undefined,
            .target = undefined,
            .previous_action = undefined,
            .hinge_qpos = undefined,
            .hinge_dof = undefined,
            .a_des = undefined,
            .torque = undefined,
            .full = undefined,
            .dense = undefined,
            .rng = undefined,
            .steps = undefined,
        };
        env.gpa = gpa;
        env.options = options;
        env.doc = try codecs.xml.parse(gpa, xml, null);
        errdefer env.doc.deinit();
        env.robot = try mjcf.readRobot(gpa, &env.doc);
        errdefer env.robot.deinit();
        var model_options: rbt.Options = .{
            .max_contacts = 256,
            .timestep = 1.0 / options.physics_hz,
            .gravity = vec(0, 0, -9.81),
        };
        model_options.solver.algorithm = .newton;
        env.imported = try robot_mjcf.build(gpa, &env.robot, model_options);
        errdefer env.imported.deinit();
        const m: *rbt.Model = &env.imported.model;
        assertf(m.jnt_type[0] == .free and m.jnt_qpos_adr[0] == 0, @src(), "the root must be a free joint 0", .{});
        // Limp: no joint springs, damping or tendon springs - the controller is the only actuator.
        @memset(m.jnt_stiffness, 0.0);
        @memset(m.jnt_damping, 0.0);
        m.has_dof_damping = false;
        @memset(m.tendon_stiffness, 0.0);
        @memset(m.tendon_damping, 0.0);

        env.data = try rbt.Data.init(gpa, m);
        errdefer env.data.deinit();
        env.tracker = try dance.Tracker.init(gpa, m.nv);
        errdefer env.tracker.deinit();

        var hinges: usize = 0;
        for (0..m.njnt) |j| {
            if (m.jnt_type[j] == .hinge) {
                hinges += 1;
            }
        }
        env.hinge_qpos = try gpa.alloc(u32, hinges);
        env.hinge_dof = try gpa.alloc(u32, hinges);
        var h: usize = 0;
        for (0..m.njnt) |j| {
            if (m.jnt_type[j] == .hinge) {
                env.hinge_qpos[h] = m.jnt_qpos_adr[j];
                env.hinge_dof[h] = m.jnt_dof_adr[j];
                h += 1;
            }
        }
        env.base = try gpa.dupe(f32, m.qpos0);
        env.target = try gpa.dupe(f32, m.qpos0);
        env.previous_action = try gpa.alloc(f32, hinges);
        env.a_des = try gpa.alloc(f32, m.nv);
        env.torque = try gpa.alloc(f32, m.nv);
        env.full = try gpa.alloc(f32, m.nv);
        env.dense = try gpa.alloc(f32, @as(usize, m.nv) * m.nv);
        // The base pose, its lowest foot point on the floor.
        @memcpy(env.data.pos, env.base);
        env.data.stage = .stale;
        rbt.forward(m, &env.data);
        env.base[2] -= dance.lowestFootPoint(m, &env.data, env.imported.names);

        env.world = try floorWorld(gpa);
        env.bridge = try robot_physics.Bridge.init(gpa, &env.world, m, &env.data, 256);
        env.bridge.listen(&env.world);
        env.rng = Random.DefaultPrng.init(0);
        env.steps = 0;
        return env;
    }

    pub fn deinit(env: *HumanoidEnv) void {
        const gpa: Allocator = env.gpa;
        env.bridge.deinit(&env.world);
        env.world.deinit(gpa);
        gpa.free(env.dense);
        gpa.free(env.full);
        gpa.free(env.torque);
        gpa.free(env.a_des);
        gpa.free(env.previous_action);
        gpa.free(env.target);
        gpa.free(env.base);
        gpa.free(env.hinge_dof);
        gpa.free(env.hinge_qpos);
        env.tracker.deinit();
        env.data.deinit();
        env.imported.deinit();
        env.robot.deinit();
        env.doc.deinit();
        gpa.destroy(env);
    }

    pub fn actionSize(env: *const HumanoidEnv) usize {
        return env.hinge_qpos.len;
    }

    pub fn observationSize(env: *const HumanoidEnv) usize {
        return 13 + 3 * env.hinge_qpos.len;
    }

    /// Start an episode: the base pose, feet on the floor, a little noise on the joints.
    ///
    /// ** A RESET MUST FORGET EVERYTHING, OR NO TWO LEARNING CURVES CAN BE COMPARED. The first
    /// version kept the physics world and the solver between episodes, and the same seed did not
    /// replay the same episode: contact caches and the solver's warm start carried the previous
    /// episode's forces into this one's first steps. The world and bridge are rebuilt and the
    /// robot's data reset - an episode is a function of its seed and its actions alone.
    pub fn reset(
        env: *HumanoidEnv,
        seed: u64,
        observation: []f32,
    ) !void {
        const m: *const rbt.Model = &env.imported.model;
        env.bridge.deinit(&env.world);
        env.world.deinit(env.gpa);
        env.data.reset(m);
        env.world = try floorWorld(env.gpa);
        env.bridge = try robot_physics.Bridge.init(env.gpa, &env.world, m, &env.data, 256);
        env.bridge.listen(&env.world);
        env.rng = Random.DefaultPrng.init(seed);
        const random: Random = env.rng.random();
        @memcpy(env.data.pos, env.base);
        @memset(env.data.vel, 0.0);
        for (env.hinge_qpos, env.hinge_dof) |q, v| {
            env.data.pos[q] += env.options.reset_noise * (2.0 * random.float(f32) - 1.0);
            env.data.vel[v] = env.options.reset_noise * (2.0 * random.float(f32) - 1.0);
        }
        env.data.stage = .stale;
        rbt.forward(m, &env.data);
        @memcpy(env.target, env.base);
        @memset(env.previous_action, 0.0);
        env.steps = 0;
        env.observe(observation);
    }

    /// One policy step: target = base + scale x clamp(action), held for `substeps` physics steps.
    pub fn step(
        env: *HumanoidEnv,
        action: []const f32,
        observation: []f32,
    ) !StepResult {
        const m: *rbt.Model = &env.imported.model;
        const d: *rbt.Data = &env.data;
        const o: Options = env.options;
        const dt: f32 = 1.0 / o.physics_hz;
        var effort: f32 = 0.0;
        for (action, env.hinge_qpos, 0..) |a, q, h| {
            const clipped: f32 = clamp(a, -1.0, 1.0);
            env.target[q] = env.base[q] + o.action_scale * clipped;
            env.previous_action[h] = clipped;
            effort += clipped * clipped;
        }
        const x_before: f32 = d.pos[0];
        for (0..o.substeps) |_| {
            rbt.forward(m, d);
            try env.bridge.sync(&env.world, m, d);
            try zimrphysics.step(&env.world, dt);
            env.bridge.harvest(d);
            // Hold the target: reference velocity and acceleration zero (all three frames equal).
            env.tracker.accelerations(m, d, .{ env.target, env.target, env.target }, o.spring_hz, dt, env.a_des);
            rbt.biasForce(m, d);
            rmx.floatingBaseTorques(m, d, env.a_des, env.dense, env.full, env.torque);
            @memset(d.applied_force, 0.0);
            for (env.hinge_dof) |v| {
                d.applied_force[v] = env.torque[v];
            }
            rbt.step(m, d);
        }
        rbt.forward(m, d);
        env.steps += 1;
        const elapsed: f32 = float(o.substeps) * dt;
        const forward_speed: f32 = (d.pos[0] - x_before) / elapsed;
        const height: f32 = d.pos[2];
        const terminated: bool = !zm.isFinite(height) or height < o.healthy_height;
        env.observe(observation);
        return .{
            .reward = o.forward_weight * forward_speed + o.healthy_reward - o.control_weight * effort,
            .terminated = terminated,
            .truncated = !terminated and env.steps >= o.max_steps,
        };
    }

    fn observe(env: *const HumanoidEnv, out: []f32) void {
        const d: *const rbt.Data = &env.data;
        assertf(out.len == env.observationSize(), @src(), "observation wants {d}, got {d}", .{
            env.observationSize(),
            out.len,
        });
        const torso: Quat = .{ d.pos[3], d.pos[4], d.pos[5], d.pos[6] };
        const gravity_local: Vec = rotate(conjugate(torso), vec(0, 0, -1));
        // The heading: the torso's forward axis, flattened onto the floor.
        const forward: Vec = rotate(torso, vec(1, 0, 0));
        const heading: Quat = quatFromAxisAngle(vec(0, 0, 1), atan2Rad(forward[1], forward[0]));
        const velocity_heading: Vec = rotate(conjugate(heading), vec(d.vel[0], d.vel[1], d.vel[2]));
        out[0] = d.pos[2];
        inline for (0..3) |k| {
            out[1 + k] = gravity_local[k];
            out[4 + k] = velocity_heading[k];
            out[7 + k] = d.vel[3 + k];
        }
        out[10] = 0;
        out[11] = 0;
        out[12] = 0;
        const n: usize = env.hinge_qpos.len;
        for (env.hinge_qpos, env.hinge_dof, 0..) |q, v, h| {
            out[13 + h] = d.pos[q];
            out[13 + n + h] = d.vel[v];
            out[13 + 2 * n + h] = env.previous_action[h];
        }
    }
};

10.6 SAC#

SAC itself - every transition kept and reused from a replay buffer, two critics and the smaller of their estimates, target critics that follow slowly, a squashed Gaussian actor whose entropy is weighed by a tuned temperature - is explained in zimrrl (zimrrl 7.3); SacAgent is its implementation here. In practice SAC needs far fewer samples than PPO, and PPO parallelises across many cheap environments more easily.

SacOptions
pub const SacOptions = struct {
    hidden: usize = 64,
    batch: usize = 128,
    replay_capacity: usize = 100_000,
    /// Adam, for actor, critics and temperature alike.
    learning_rate: f64 = 3.0e-4,
    gamma: f32 = 0.99,
    /// Polyak rate for the target critics.
    tau: f32 = 0.005,
    /// Uniformly random actions before learning starts.
    warmup: usize = 1000,
    seed: u64 = 1,
    /// OBSERVATIONS NORMALISED AT SAMPLE TIME: running statistics (`zrl.ObsNormalizer`,
    /// f64 Welford) fed from every observation the agent acts on in training; the replay keeps RAW rows, and each
    /// sampled batch's observations and next observations are normalised on the batch's copy with the statistics of
    /// that moment - so a stored row never goes stale as the statistics move. Acting normalises its input the same
    /// way; a deterministic (evaluation) action reads the statistics without feeding them. Off: raw observations
    /// everywhere, the agent exactly as before.
    normalize_observations: bool = false,
    /// With the normaliser on: normalised values are clamped to this many standard deviations.
    obs_clip: f64 = 5.0,
};
AdamSet
/// Adam over a list of tensors: a moment and a velocity each, and a step count.
pub const AdamSet = struct {
    moments: []zn.Tensor(f32),
    velocities: []zn.Tensor(f32),
    step: usize = 0,

    pub fn init(arena: Allocator, weights: []const zn.Tensor(f32)) !AdamSet {
        const moments: []zn.Tensor(f32) = try arena.alloc(zn.Tensor(f32), weights.len);
        const velocities: []zn.Tensor(f32) = try arena.alloc(zn.Tensor(f32), weights.len);
        for (weights, moments, velocities) |w, *mo, *ve| {
            mo.* = try zn.Tensor(f32).alloc(arena, w.shape[0..w.rank]);
            ve.* = try zn.Tensor(f32).alloc(arena, w.shape[0..w.rank]);
            @memset(mo.data, 0.0);
            @memset(ve.data, 0.0);
        }
        return .{ .moments = moments, .velocities = velocities };
    }

    pub fn apply(
        self: *AdamSet,
        g: *zn.Graph(f32),
        weights: []const zn.Tensor(f32),
        vars: []const zn.Var,
        rate: f64,
    ) !void {
        self.step += 1;
        const hyper: zn.Adam = .{ .rate = rate };
        for (weights, vars, self.moments, self.velocities) |w, v, mo, ve| {
            try zn.adamStep(f32, w, w, try g.gradOf(v), mo, ve, hyper, self.step);
        }
    }
};
SacAgent
/// Soft Actor-Critic (Haarnoja et al. 2018), assembled from zimrnum's parts: a tanh-squashed
/// Gaussian actor (`squashedReparameterize`), twin critics on `concat(s, a)` with polyak targets,
/// the target y = r + gamma (1 - done)(min Q' - alpha log pi), and a tuned temperature
/// (`zrl.Temperature`). Every network steps ADAM: zimrnum's `offPolicyUpdate` steps plain SGD,
/// the trap `ppoUpdate` already sprang (rl_track_journal.md section 6). Env-agnostic: flat observations
/// and actions in [-1, 1].
pub const SacAgent = struct {
    arena_state: ArenaAllocator,
    gpa: Allocator,
    options: SacOptions,
    n_obs: usize,
    n_act: usize,
    actor: Mlp3,
    /// The log-std, one learned row [1, n_act] before its tanh bound: zimrnum's
    /// `squashedReparameterize` takes a state-INDEPENDENT log-std (shape [1, dims]) - a common,
    /// workable SAC variant; a per-row log-std is a small library extension for later.
    raw_log_std: zn.Tensor(f32),
    raw_log_std_var: zn.Var = undefined,
    q1: Mlp3,
    q2: Mlp3,
    target1: Mlp3,
    target2: Mlp3,
    critic_graph: zn.Graph(f32),
    critic_obs: zn.Var,
    critic_act: zn.Var,
    critic_y: zn.Var,
    critic_loss: zn.Var,
    /// The critics' parameter handles IN THE CRITIC GRAPH. A `Var` indexes one graph, and a
    /// `Layer` keeps only its last `apply`'s handles - the actor graph re-applies the critics,
    /// so without this capture the critic step read the actor graph's indices (out of bounds).
    critic_vars: [12]zn.Var,
    actor_graph: zn.Graph(f32),
    actor_obs: zn.Var,
    actor_noise: zn.Tensor(f32),
    actor_alpha: zn.Var,
    actor_log_prob: zn.Var,
    actor_loss: zn.Var,
    critic_adam: AdamSet,
    actor_adam: AdamSet,
    temperature: zrl.Temperature,
    alpha_moment: f64 = 0,
    alpha_velocity: f64 = 0,
    replay: zrl.ReplayBuffer(f32),
    rng: Random.DefaultPrng,
    updates: usize = 0,
    // plain-forward scratch
    row: []f32,
    t1: []f32,
    t2: []f32,
    out: []f32,
    qin: []f32,
    q_out: []f32,
    /// A drawn batch (replay rows) and the noise for its next actions: `update` fills them and
    /// hands them to `updateWith`, which a check can call with its own.
    batch_rows: []f32,
    next_noise: []f32,
    /// The observation normaliser (`normalize_observations`), or null when it is off. It works in f64 (its running
    /// mean over millions of observations would stall in f32), so `normalizer_in` / `normalizer_out` carry one
    /// observation across; `normalized_obs` is the normalised observation acting hands the policy.
    obs_normalizer: ?zrl.ObsNormalizer,
    normalizer_in: []f64,
    normalizer_out: []f64,
    normalized_obs: []f32,
    /// One action's noise, for `policy`.
    noise_row: []f32,

    pub fn init(
        gpa: Allocator,
        n_obs: usize,
        n_act: usize,
        options: SacOptions,
    ) !*SacAgent {
        const a: *SacAgent = try gpa.create(SacAgent);
        errdefer gpa.destroy(a);
        // whole-init-first: the whole struct first - defaults applied, every field named.
        a.* = .{
            .arena_state = undefined,
            .gpa = undefined,
            .options = undefined,
            .n_obs = undefined,
            .n_act = undefined,
            .actor = undefined,
            .raw_log_std = undefined,
            .q1 = undefined,
            .q2 = undefined,
            .target1 = undefined,
            .target2 = undefined,
            .critic_graph = undefined,
            .critic_obs = undefined,
            .critic_act = undefined,
            .critic_y = undefined,
            .critic_loss = undefined,
            .critic_vars = undefined,
            .actor_graph = undefined,
            .actor_obs = undefined,
            .actor_noise = undefined,
            .actor_alpha = undefined,
            .actor_log_prob = undefined,
            .actor_loss = undefined,
            .critic_adam = undefined,
            .actor_adam = undefined,
            .temperature = undefined,
            .replay = undefined,
            .rng = undefined,
            .row = undefined,
            .t1 = undefined,
            .t2 = undefined,
            .out = undefined,
            .qin = undefined,
            .q_out = undefined,
            .batch_rows = undefined,
            .next_noise = undefined,
            .noise_row = undefined,
            .obs_normalizer = null,
            .normalizer_in = undefined,
            .normalizer_out = undefined,
            .normalized_obs = undefined,
        };
        a.arena_state = ArenaAllocator.init(gpa);
        errdefer a.arena_state.deinit();
        const arena: Allocator = a.arena_state.allocator();
        a.gpa = gpa;
        a.options = options;
        a.n_obs = n_obs;
        a.n_act = n_act;
        a.alpha_moment = 0;
        a.alpha_velocity = 0;
        a.updates = 0;
        a.rng = Random.DefaultPrng.init(options.seed);
        const random: Random = a.rng.random();
        const h: usize = options.hidden;
        const b: usize = options.batch;
        a.actor = try Mlp3.init(arena, random, n_obs, h, n_act, 0.01);
        a.raw_log_std = try zeros(arena, &.{ 1, n_act });
        a.q1 = try Mlp3.init(arena, random, n_obs + n_act, h, 1, 1.0);
        a.q2 = try Mlp3.init(arena, random, n_obs + n_act, h, 1, 1.0);
        a.target1 = try Mlp3.init(arena, random, n_obs + n_act, h, 1, 1.0);
        a.target2 = try Mlp3.init(arena, random, n_obs + n_act, h, 1, 1.0);
        for (a.target1.tensors(), a.q1.tensors()) |t, o| {
            @memcpy(t.data, o.data);
        }
        for (a.target2.tensors(), a.q2.tensors()) |t, o| {
            @memcpy(t.data, o.data);
        }
        // *** -1 PER DIMENSION, the SAC heuristic (target entropy = per_dim x action_dim). This
        // passed +1.0 at first: a target entropy of +1, which a tanh-squashed 1-D action cannot
        // reach (its maximum is the uniform's, log 2 ~ 0.69) - so alpha rose from the first update
        // and ran away, doubling every 2k steps, and the cartpole policy collapsed after 8k.
        a.temperature = try zrl.Temperature.forActionDim(n_act, -1.0);

        const ones_t: zn.Tensor(f32) = try .alloc(arena, &.{ b, 1 });
        @memset(ones_t.data, 1.0);
        const mean_row_t: zn.Tensor(f32) = try .alloc(arena, &.{ 1, b });
        @memset(mean_row_t.data, 1.0 / float(b));

        // -- The critic graph: both critics against one target column. --
        a.critic_graph = zn.Graph(f32).init(arena);
        a.critic_graph.useScratchAllocator(gpa);
        const cg: *zn.Graph(f32) = &a.critic_graph;
        a.critic_obs = try cg.constant(try zeros(arena, &.{ b, n_obs }));
        a.critic_act = try cg.constant(try zeros(arena, &.{ b, n_act }));
        a.critic_y = try cg.constant(try zeros(arena, &.{ b, 1 }));
        const c_ones: zn.Var = try cg.constant(ones_t);
        const sa: zn.Var = try cg.concat(a.critic_obs, a.critic_act, 1);
        const v1: zn.Var = try a.q1.apply(cg, sa, c_ones);
        const v2: zn.Var = try a.q2.apply(cg, sa, c_ones);
        a.critic_loss = try cg.add(try cg.mseLoss(v1, a.critic_y), try cg.mseLoss(v2, a.critic_y));
        a.critic_vars = concatVars(a.q1.vars(), a.q2.vars());

        // -- The actor graph: a reparameterised draw through the (shared) critics. --
        a.actor_graph = zn.Graph(f32).init(arena);
        a.actor_graph.useScratchAllocator(gpa);
        const ag: *zn.Graph(f32) = &a.actor_graph;
        a.actor_obs = try ag.constant(try zeros(arena, &.{ b, n_obs }));
        const a_ones: zn.Var = try ag.constant(ones_t);
        const mean: zn.Var = try a.actor.apply(ag, a.actor_obs, a_ones);
        a.raw_log_std_var = try ag.parameter(a.raw_log_std);
        const raw_log_std: zn.Var = a.raw_log_std_var;
        const half_span: f32 = 0.5 * (log_std_max - log_std_min);
        const offset_t: zn.Tensor(f32) = try .alloc(arena, &.{ 1, n_act });
        @memset(offset_t.data, log_std_min + half_span);
        const log_std_span: zn.Var = try ag.scale(try ag.tanh(raw_log_std), half_span);
        const log_std: zn.Var = try ag.add(log_std_span, try ag.constant(offset_t));
        a.actor_noise = try zeros(arena, &.{ b, n_act });
        const draw: zn.SquashedDraw = try ag.squashedReparameterize(mean, log_std, a.actor_noise);
        a.actor_log_prob = draw.log_prob;
        const q_in: zn.Var = try ag.concat(a.actor_obs, draw.action, 1);
        const w1: zn.Var = try a.q1.apply(ag, q_in, a_ones);
        const w2: zn.Var = try a.q2.apply(ag, q_in, a_ones);
        a.actor_alpha = try ag.constant(try zeros(arena, &.{ b, 1 }));
        const per_sample: zn.Var = try ag.sub(try ag.mul(a.actor_alpha, draw.log_prob), try ag.min(w1, w2));
        a.actor_loss = try ag.matmul(try ag.constant(mean_row_t), per_sample);

        a.critic_adam = try AdamSet.init(arena, &concatTensors(a.q1.tensors(), a.q2.tensors()));
        a.actor_adam = try AdamSet.init(arena, &(a.actor.tensors() ++ [1]zn.Tensor(f32){a.raw_log_std}));
        a.replay = try zrl.ReplayBuffer(f32).init(arena, options.replay_capacity, 2 * n_obs + n_act + 2);
        a.row = try arena.alloc(f32, 2 * n_obs + n_act + 2);
        a.t1 = try arena.alloc(f32, h);
        a.t2 = try arena.alloc(f32, h);
        a.out = try arena.alloc(f32, n_act);
        a.qin = try arena.alloc(f32, n_obs + n_act);
        a.q_out = try arena.alloc(f32, 1);
        a.batch_rows = try arena.alloc(f32, b * (2 * n_obs + n_act + 2));
        a.next_noise = try arena.alloc(f32, b * n_act);
        a.noise_row = try arena.alloc(f32, n_act);
        a.normalizer_in = try arena.alloc(f64, n_obs);
        a.normalizer_out = try arena.alloc(f64, n_obs);
        a.normalized_obs = try arena.alloc(f32, n_obs);
        if (options.normalize_observations) {
            // In the agent's arena, freed with it. Its clip is ours (5 deviations), not its own default (10).
            var normalizer: zrl.ObsNormalizer = try .init(arena, n_obs);
            normalizer.clip = options.obs_clip;
            a.obs_normalizer = normalizer;
        }
        return a;
    }

    pub fn deinit(a: *SacAgent) void {
        a.critic_graph.deinitScratch();
        a.actor_graph.deinitScratch();
        a.arena_state.deinit();
        a.gpa.destroy(a);
    }

    fn zeros(arena: Allocator, shape: []const usize) !zn.Tensor(f32) {
        const t: zn.Tensor(f32) = try .alloc(arena, shape);
        @memset(t.data, 0.0);
        return t;
    }

    fn concatTensors(x: [6]zn.Tensor(f32), y: [6]zn.Tensor(f32)) [12]zn.Tensor(f32) {
        return x ++ y;
    }

    /// `policy` with the noise given (one value per action dimension), not drawn.
    fn policyWithNoise(
        a: *SacAgent,
        obs: []const f32,
        action: []f32,
        noise: []const f32,
    ) f32 {
        a.actor.forward(obs, a.t1, a.t2, a.out);
        var log_prob: f32 = 0.0;
        for (0..a.n_act) |k| {
            const half_span: f32 = 0.5 * (log_std_max - log_std_min);
            const ls: f32 = log_std_min + half_span + half_span * tanh(a.raw_log_std.data[k]);
            const u: f32 = a.out[k] + @exp(ls) * noise[k];
            action[k] = tanh(u);
            log_prob += -0.5 * noise[k] * noise[k] - ls - 0.5 * @log(2.0 * pi) - zn.squashCorrection(f32, u);
        }
        return log_prob;
    }

    /// The actor's action for one observation, in [-1, 1], and its log-prob: a draw, or the
    /// mean (`deterministic`) - what the policy has learned, for evaluation.
    fn policy(
        a: *SacAgent,
        obs: []const f32,
        action: []f32,
        deterministic: bool,
    ) f32 {
        // One copy of the actor's forward and log-prob (`policyWithNoise`): the noise is drawn
        // here, one value per dimension in order - the same stream this drew inline before.
        for (a.noise_row) |*x| {
            x.* = if (deterministic) 0.0 else a.rng.random().floatNorm(f32);
        }
        return a.policyWithNoise(obs, action, a.noise_row);
    }

    /// The action for `obs`, into `action`. In training (`deterministic` false): a uniform random action while the
    /// replay is still inside its warm-up, the policy's draw after that. In an evaluation (`deterministic`): the
    /// policy's mean, never random. With the normaliser on, every TRAINING observation also feeds its statistics -
    /// warm-up ones too, they are the start of the data - and the policy always sees the observation normalised with
    /// the statistics as they stand. An evaluation only reads them: judging a policy must not change what it sees next.
    pub fn act(
        a: *SacAgent,
        obs: []const f32,
        action: []f32,
        deterministic: bool,
    ) void {
        if (!deterministic) {
            a.feedNormalizer(obs);
        }
        if (!deterministic and a.replay.len < a.options.warmup) {
            for (action) |*x| {
                x.* = 2.0 * a.rng.random().float(f32) - 1.0;
            }
            return;
        }
        const policy_input: []const f32 = a.normalized(obs);
        _ = a.policy(policy_input, action, deterministic);
    }

    /// With the normaliser on: `obs` into its running statistics. Off: nothing.
    fn feedNormalizer(a: *SacAgent, obs: []const f32) void {
        if (a.obs_normalizer) |*normalizer| {
            widen(obs, a.normalizer_in);
            // The lengths match by construction; a mismatch here is a bug, not an input.
            normalizer.observe(a.normalizer_in) catch |err| {
                assertUnreachable(@src(), "observation normaliser: {s}", .{@errorName(err)});
            };
        }
    }

    /// `obs` as the policy should see it: normalised with the statistics as they stand (into `normalized_obs`), or
    /// `obs` itself when the normaliser is off.
    fn normalized(a: *SacAgent, obs: []const f32) []const f32 {
        if (a.obs_normalizer == null) {
            return obs;
        }
        a.normalizeInto(obs, a.normalized_obs);
        return a.normalized_obs;
    }

    /// `obs` normalised into `out` with the statistics as they stand - in place is fine (`out` may be `obs`): the
    /// values cross into f64 scratch first, because `ObsNormalizer` works in f64.
    fn normalizeInto(a: *SacAgent, obs: []const f32, out: []f32) void {
        widen(obs, a.normalizer_in);
        a.obs_normalizer.?.apply(a.normalizer_in, a.normalizer_out) catch |err| {
            assertUnreachable(@src(), "observation normaliser: {s}", .{@errorName(err)});
        };
        for (out, a.normalizer_out) |*to, x| {
            to.* = @floatCast(x);
        }
    }

    /// An f32 observation into f64 scratch of the same length.
    fn widen(from: []const f32, into: []f64) void {
        for (into, from) |*to, x| {
            to.* = x;
        }
    }

    /// Store one transition. `done` is a TERMINATION (no bootstrap), not a truncation. The row keeps the DISCOUNT
    /// that multiplies the bootstrap - for a one-step row, `gamma * (1 - done)`: gamma, or zero after a termination.
    pub fn remember(
        a: *SacAgent,
        obs: []const f32,
        action: []const f32,
        reward: f32,
        next: []const f32,
        done: bool,
    ) !void {
        const done_f: f32 = if (done) 1.0 else 0.0;
        try a.rememberDiscounted(obs, action, reward, next, a.options.gamma * (1.0 - done_f));
    }

    /// Store one transition whose bootstrap discount is given - an n-step row: `reward` is the window's discounted
    /// return, `next` where it bootstraps from, `discount` gamma^k (zero when the window ended in a termination).
    /// The target is `reward + discount * (min Q' - alpha log pi')`.
    pub fn rememberDiscounted(
        a: *SacAgent,
        obs: []const f32,
        action: []const f32,
        reward: f32,
        next: []const f32,
        discount: f32,
    ) !void {
        const n_obs: usize = a.n_obs;
        @memcpy(a.row[0..n_obs], obs);
        @memcpy(a.row[n_obs..][0..a.n_act], action);
        a.row[n_obs + a.n_act] = reward;
        @memcpy(a.row[n_obs + a.n_act + 1 ..][0..n_obs], next);
        a.row[2 * n_obs + a.n_act + 1] = discount;
        try a.replay.push(a.row);
    }

    fn criticMin(
        net1: *const Mlp3,
        net2: *const Mlp3,
        a: *SacAgent,
    ) f32 {
        net1.forward(a.qin, a.t1, a.t2, a.q_out);
        const first: f32 = a.q_out[0];
        net2.forward(a.qin, a.t1, a.t2, a.q_out);
        return @min(first, a.q_out[0]);
    }

    /// One SAC update from a replayed batch, once the warm-up is past.
    pub fn update(a: *SacAgent) !void {
        if (a.replay.len < @max(a.options.warmup, a.options.batch)) {
            return;
        }
        try a.sampleBatch();
        for (a.next_noise) |*x| {
            x.* = a.rng.random().floatNorm(f32);
        }
        for (a.actor_noise.data) |*x| {
            x.* = a.rng.random().floatNorm(f32);
        }
        try a.updateWith(a.batch_rows, a.next_noise, a.actor_noise.data);
    }

    /// Draw this update's batch into `batch_rows` - and, with the normaliser on, normalise the batch's observations
    /// and next observations THERE, with the statistics of this moment: the replay's rows stay raw, so none of them
    /// goes stale as the statistics move. Normaliser off: exactly the draw `update` always made.
    pub fn sampleBatch(a: *SacAgent) !void {
        const n_obs: usize = a.n_obs;
        const width: usize = 2 * n_obs + a.n_act + 2;
        const sample_rng: zn.Rng = .init(@truncate(a.updates *% 2654435761));
        for (0..a.options.batch) |i| {
            try a.replay.sample(sample_rng, @intCast(i), a.batch_rows[i * width ..][0..width]);
        }
        if (a.obs_normalizer == null) {
            return;
        }
        for (0..a.options.batch) |i| {
            const row: []f32 = a.batch_rows[i * width ..][0..width];
            a.normalizeInto(row[0..n_obs], row[0..n_obs]);
            const next: []f32 = row[n_obs + a.n_act + 1 ..][0..n_obs];
            a.normalizeInto(next, next);
        }
    }

    /// One SAC update from the given batch (replay rows: obs, action, reward, next obs, discount)
    /// and noise (next actions', then the actor's; [batch, n_act] each).
    pub fn updateWith(
        a: *SacAgent,
        rows: []const f32,
        next_noise: []const f32,
        actor_noise: []const f32,
    ) !void {
        const b: usize = a.options.batch;
        const width: usize = 2 * a.n_obs + a.n_act + 2;
        const n_obs: usize = a.n_obs;
        const n_act: usize = a.n_act;
        const cg: *zn.Graph(f32) = &a.critic_graph;
        const ag: *zn.Graph(f32) = &a.actor_graph;
        const obs_c: []f32 = cg.valueOf(a.critic_obs).data;
        const act_c: []f32 = cg.valueOf(a.critic_act).data;
        const y: []f32 = cg.valueOf(a.critic_y).data;
        const obs_a: []f32 = ag.valueOf(a.actor_obs).data;
        const alpha: f32 = @floatCast(a.temperature.alpha());
        const next_action: []f32 = a.out[0..n_act];
        for (0..b) |i| {
            const row: []const f32 = rows[i * width ..][0..width];
            const obs: []const f32 = row[0..n_obs];
            const action: []const f32 = row[n_obs..][0..n_act];
            const reward: f32 = row[n_obs + n_act];
            const next: []const f32 = row[n_obs + n_act + 1 ..][0..n_obs];
            const discount: f32 = row[2 * n_obs + n_act + 1];
            @memcpy(obs_c[i * n_obs ..][0..n_obs], obs);
            @memcpy(obs_a[i * n_obs ..][0..n_obs], obs);
            @memcpy(act_c[i * n_act ..][0..n_act], action);
            // The target: a' ~ pi(s'), then the pessimistic target critics.
            var action_buf: [64]f32 = undefined;
            const noise: []const f32 = next_noise[i * n_act ..][0..n_act];
            const next_log_prob: f32 = a.policyWithNoise(next, action_buf[0..n_act], noise);
            @memcpy(a.qin[0..n_obs], next);
            @memcpy(a.qin[n_obs..][0..n_act], action_buf[0..n_act]);
            const q_next: f32 = criticMin(&a.target1, &a.target2, a);
            y[i] = reward + discount * (q_next - alpha * next_log_prob);
        }
        _ = next_action;
        try cg.recompute();
        try cg.backward(a.critic_loss);
        try a.critic_adam.apply(
            cg,
            &concatTensors(a.q1.tensors(), a.q2.tensors()),
            &a.critic_vars,
            a.options.learning_rate,
        );

        // The actor: fresh noise, the current alpha, gradients through the critics to the action.
        if (actor_noise.ptr != a.actor_noise.data.ptr) {
            @memcpy(a.actor_noise.data, actor_noise);
        }
        @memset(ag.valueOf(a.actor_alpha).data, alpha);
        try ag.recompute();
        try ag.backward(a.actor_loss);
        try a.actor_adam.apply(
            ag,
            &(a.actor.tensors() ++ [1]zn.Tensor(f32){a.raw_log_std}),
            &(a.actor.vars() ++ [1]zn.Var{a.raw_log_std_var}),
            a.options.learning_rate,
        );

        // The temperature, toward its target entropy (Adam on log alpha, by hand: one scalar).
        var mean_log_prob: f64 = 0.0;
        for (ag.valueOf(a.actor_log_prob).data) |lp| {
            mean_log_prob += lp;
        }
        mean_log_prob /= float64(b);
        const grad: f64 = a.temperature.gradient(mean_log_prob);
        a.alpha_moment = 0.9 * a.alpha_moment + 0.1 * grad;
        a.alpha_velocity = 0.999 * a.alpha_velocity + 0.001 * grad * grad;
        const t: f64 = float64(a.updates + 1);
        const m_hat: f64 = a.alpha_moment / (1.0 - @exp(t * @log(0.9)));
        const v_hat: f64 = a.alpha_velocity / (1.0 - @exp(t * @log(0.999)));
        a.temperature.log_alpha -= a.options.learning_rate * m_hat / (@sqrt(v_hat) + 1.0e-8);

        // The targets follow.
        for (a.target1.tensors(), a.q1.tensors()) |target, online| {
            try zn.polyakUpdate(f32, target, online, a.options.tau);
        }
        for (a.target2.tensors(), a.q2.tensors()) |target, online| {
            try zn.polyakUpdate(f32, target, online, a.options.tau);
        }
        a.updates += 1;
    }

    fn concatVars(x: [6]zn.Var, y: [6]zn.Var) [12]zn.Var {
        return x ++ y;
    }
};

10.7 A tracker trained in a page#

examples/getup_train puts all of this in a page: the characters stepped on the device's CPU, the policy and value networks trained on its GPU, and nothing pre-trained anywhere — every weight it uses is learned where it runs, or uploaded by whoever runs it. Build it as one self-contained file with zig build getup-train -Dplatform=web -Dmode=release and open zig-out/standalone/getup_train.html on a phone. Two motions are on offer, switched with a button: getting up off the floor (five seconds, contact-rich) and dancing (twenty seconds of continuous balance).

The number it shows is the mean time to failure: how long a character tracks, on average, before it loses the reference. That is not the same as how long episodes last. Characters start at random points of the clip, so an episode can never outlast what is left of the clip — on a five-second clip that averages two and a half seconds, so "episode length" tops out well below perfect however good the policy is. Counting failures against the time characters were watched does not have that ceiling: running out of clip while still with the reference is survival, not failure, and a perfect tracker's number grows without limit. The servo alone is measured the same way, on the device, before learning starts — and because the measure does not depend on the clip's length, both motions share milestones: the minutes of training until characters lose the reference only every 2, 5, 10 and 20 seconds, counted only once the helping hand has faded.

The clips arrive baked: retargeted, filtered, cut and lifted once, offline, by zig build clip-bake, into a few hundred kilobytes of floats. The page loads them instantly — no inverse kinematics at startup — and they are exactly the numbers the page used to compute, because the baker runs the same functions and checks what it wrote against them.

Two buttons keep a run: save downloads the newest weights as a file named by motion and by how many batches trained them, and load carries on from such a file — or refuses it by name, if it is not weights, belongs to a network of another shape, or was trained for the other motion. Both are covered by real, invisible page elements rather than drawn buttons alone, because a phone only saves or opens a file from inside a genuine tap.

takeUploads
/// Weights the user picked: carried on from if they fit this network AND this motion, refused by
/// name if not.
fn takeUploads(s: *State) void {
    while (z.userfile.pendingCount() > 0) {
        const size: u32 = z.userfile.nextSize();
        const bytes: []u8 = s.gpa.alloc(u8, size) catch {
            z.userfile.discardNext();
            return;
        };
        defer s.gpa.free(bytes);
        _ = z.userfile.readNext(bytes);
        if (s.trainer.importWeights(bytes)) |_| {
            // A fresh record from here: the servo stands, the history and milestones restart.
            const servo_exposure: u64 = s.progress.servo_exposure;
            const servo_failures: u32 = s.progress.servo_failures;
            s.progress = .{};
            s.progress.servo_left = 0;
            s.progress.servo_exposure = servo_exposure;
            s.progress.servo_failures = servo_failures;
            setStatus(s, "loaded batch {d}", .{s.trainer.iterations});
            offerWeights(s);
        } else |err| {
            setStatus(s, "refused: {s}", .{@errorName(err)});
        }
    }
}

On Geno, every setting of this training - the characters at once, the batch's length, the networks' width, the learning rate, the initial exploration, the assist's schedule, the action scale and DReCon's filter - is one value, PPO's recipe on Geno, with each field defaulted to the training page's choice. The page builds its trainer from it, joined to Geno's task and DReCon bodies, so anything else that trains or shows a Geno policy starts from the same settings:

PpoRecipe
/// PPO's recipe on Geno: every scalar of the trainer's options (`ppo_track.Options`), each defaulted to the value the
/// training page trains with. `options` joins it to Geno's task and bodies.
///
/// PPO learns in BATCHES. Every character acts for `horizon` decisions with the current policy, sampling its actions
/// around the policy's mean; the batch - `envs` x `horizon` decisions, each with its observation, action, reward and
/// how its episode went on - is turned into ADVANTAGES (how much better each action did than the critic expected,
/// `gamma` and `lambda`), and the policy is updated on it for `epochs` passes of `minibatch` rows. Then the batch is
/// thrown away and the next one collected with the updated policy: PPO learns only from what its current policy did.
pub const PpoRecipe = struct {
    /// Characters acting side by side, each its own episodes - vectorised environments. More characters give each
    /// batch more varied experience (different moments of the clip, different stumbles) and so steadier updates,
    /// for more simulation per batch. Eight keep a batch's decisions inside a phone's frames; a desktop takes many
    /// more.
    envs: u32 = 8,
    /// Decisions each character makes per batch: the rollout's length. With `envs` it sets the batch's size
    /// (8 x 64 = 512 decisions). A longer rollout lets an advantage see further before it must lean on the critic at
    /// the rollout's end, and leaves the data a little staler by the time it is learned from.
    horizon: u32 = 64,
    /// Passes over each batch, and the rows each gradient step of a pass takes. PPO reuses a batch for several
    /// passes - more learning from the same simulation - and its clipped objective keeps every pass's policy close to
    /// the one that collected the data, which is what makes reuse safe.
    epochs: u32 = 4,
    minibatch: u32 = 256,
    /// The DISCOUNT: a reward k decisions ahead counts gamma^k as much as one now. Credit reaches about
    /// 1 / (1 - gamma) decisions ahead: 100 decisions, 3.3 seconds at 30 decisions a second - long enough for a
    /// stumble's cost to reach the decision that caused it.
    gamma: f32 = 0.99,
    /// GAE's lambda (Generalised Advantage Estimation): how an advantage blends the critic's one-step estimate - the
    /// reward now plus the critic's value of the next state, steady but as wrong as the critic (lambda 0) - with the
    /// whole discounted return that followed, right on average but noisy (lambda 1). 0.95 leans toward the return
    /// while cutting most of its noise: the value nearly every PPO uses.
    lambda: f32 = 0.95,
    /// What the clip running out counts as (`ppo_track.ClipEnd`): the end of the story, with nothing after it to
    /// value, or the end of the tape while the character was doing fine, valued as if it went on.
    clip_end: ppo_track.ClipEnd = .terminal,
    /// The width of both networks' two hidden layers - the actor's and the critic's. One clip is a small function;
    /// small networks learn it faster at first (DReCon's figure 8).
    hidden: u32 = 48,
    /// Adam's step size, for both networks.
    learning_rate: f32 = 3.0e-4,
    /// Exploration at the start: log sigma -1.2, a Gaussian of 0.3 action units - 0.36 rad of raw offset at
    /// `student_scale`, 4 degrees at the joint once DReCon's filter has taken its fifth.
    initial_log_std: f32 = -1.2,
    /// Inputs normalised by their running mean and spread (`zrl.ObsNormalizer`, Welford's statistics):
    /// every input a Z-score of the same size, whatever its unit.
    normalize: bool = true,
    /// A CURRICULUM: a helping hand that holds the character's root up, this strong at the first batch and fading to
    /// nothing over `assist_batches`. Early on an untrained policy falls at once and learns little from it; held up,
    /// it lives long enough to learn what tracking is, and the hand fades before it can learn to lean on it.
    assist_start: f32 = 1.0,
    assist_batches: u32 = 300,
    /// Episodes end here even while tracking is fine, in physics steps: longer than the dance's twenty seconds.
    max_episode_steps: u32 = 1300,
    /// Radians of raw pose offset per unit of action (`student_scale`, where the reasoning lives).
    action_scale: f32 = student_scale,
    /// Physics steps a decision is held (30 Hz decisions over 60 Hz physics), and DReCon's filter: the share of
    /// a new action a joint receives each decision.
    decimation: u32 = 2,
    beta: f32 = 0.2,
    seed: u64 = 1,

    /// The trainer's options for `motion`: Geno's task and DReCon bodies, the motion's tag, and every field of this
    /// recipe - each the trainer's option of the same name, copied by one loop, so that a field added to the recipe
    /// reaches the trainer or fails to compile, and is never left behind.
    pub fn options(recipe: PpoRecipe, motion: GenoMotion) ppo_track.Options {
        var trainer_options: ppo_track.Options = .{
            .task = tracking_task,
            .bodies = drecon_bodies,
            .tag = motion.tag(),
        };
        inline for (@typeInfo(PpoRecipe).@"struct".field_names) |field_name| {
            @field(trainer_options, field_name) = @field(recipe, field_name);
        }
        return trainer_options;
    }
};

The same training on Geno, examples/geno_ppo, is the one meant to run through a night, unattended, and it keeps a run by itself. After the first batch, and then every five minutes of training, it saves the newest weights and a training log as saved values - in the browser's storage on the web, as files in the program's folder under the user's application data on a computer (%APPDATA%\zimr\geno_ppo on Windows). At start-up it carries on from them without asking: a run that crashed at two in the morning resumes where its last autosave left it. start over discards them.

   start-up    an autosave of this network and motion?   yes -> resume from its batch      no -> from scratch
               (the servo is measured alone either way)
   training    after the first batch, then every 5 minutes of training:
                   get-up.weights     the newest weights: both networks, Adam's state, the normaliser
                   get-up.log.csv     one line per batch
   morning     the weights carry on in the page, or load into another; the log opens in a spreadsheet

The log holds raw counts rather than conclusions, so that any measure can be worked out afterwards - the mean time to failure over any window is the steps watched divided by the failures, in seconds at 60 steps a second:

   batch,training_minutes,steps,steps_watched,failures,mean_reward,episodes,mean_episode_steps,assist
   1,0.00,1024,1024,0,0.35630,2,73.0,1.000
resumeFromAutosave
/// Carries on from this motion's autosave, if there is one this network accepts: its weights - and with them its
/// batch count, Adam's state and the normaliser's statistics - and its training log. Out of memory fails the start:
/// a log not carried on would be overwritten, empty, at the next autosave.
fn resumeFromAutosave(
    gpa: Allocator,
    trainer: *Trainer,
    task: Task,
    training_log: *ArrayList(u8),
    most_log_bytes: usize,
) Allocator.Error!ResumeOutcome {
    var key_buffer: [48]u8 = undefined;
    const weights_buffer: []u8 = try gpa.alloc(u8, trainer.weightsByteCount());
    defer gpa.free(weights_buffer);
    const saved_weights: []u8 = z.loadValue(autosaveKey(task, ".weights", &key_buffer), weights_buffer) orelse
        return .nothing_saved;
    trainer.importWeights(saved_weights) catch |err| {
        return .{ .refused = @errorName(err) };
    };
    const log_buffer: []u8 = try gpa.alloc(u8, most_log_bytes);
    defer gpa.free(log_buffer);
    if (z.loadValue(autosaveKey(task, ".log.csv", &key_buffer), log_buffer)) |saved_log| {
        training_log.clearRetainingCapacity();
        try training_log.appendSlice(gpa, saved_log);
    }
    return .resumed;
}

A run need not live in a page at all. geno_trainer trains the same recipe headless - no window, no frames, as fast as the GPU and the CPU allow - in a run folder, which holds everything about the run, so that another program can watch it while it goes and anyone can carry it on later:

   ../geno_runs/night1/
       run.zon         the run's parameters: the motion, the recipe, when to save and when to stop
       weights          the newest weights, rewritten whole every few minutes
       weights_b0012000 a checkpoint: the weights after batch 12,000
       policy           the newest policy, written with the weights: what the lab plays
       policy_m00090    a checkpoint: the policy after 90 minutes of training
       log.csv          one line per batch, the counts above
       judge.csv        the servo judged, then the newest policy every few minutes
       status.zon       its state, batches, minutes, the servo's and the recent time to failure
       stop             created by anyone: the trainer saves everything and exits

   geno_trainer --run=../geno_runs/night1

A SuperTrack run lives in a folder of the same shape: the same run.zon, policy, status.zon and stop, with a state and a log of its own, because SuperTrack learns in a different unit. A round is every character simulating collect steps from the policy's CPU mirror, with exploration noise, then one update of the world model and one of the policy on windows the GPU gathers from its ring:

   ../geno_runs/supertrack1/
       supertrack_state  the whole learner: both networks, Adam's moments, the counters, the random stream
       policy            the newest policy, written with the state (SuperTrack's features, every step, no filter)
       log.csv           one line per round: round, minutes, steps watched, failures, both update counts
       policy_m00090     a checkpoint: the policy after 90 minutes of training, as every learner's run keeps them
       judge.csv         the servo judged, then the newest policy every few minutes - the same judge as PPO's
       status.zon        as a PPO run's: its state, rounds, minutes, the servo's and the recent time to failure

The trainer builds the fleet on SuperTrack's training task - Geno's task with a training window's grace after every reset - measures the servo alone on it, measures the features' normaliser from the reference clip, and makes the learner. Started again on the same folder, it loads the state; the replay is not kept, so its first round or two only collect, refilling the ring, before the updates resume. A state of another shape or other options is refused, naming the first setting that differs, and the folder is left untouched.

Resuming on a GPU has one trap. The weights come back to the CPU through a readback that lands a frame or so after it is started, and a copy started before the saved weights were uploaded would bring back the weights the upload replaced - the mirror the characters act from would go back to the fresh learner's for a round. Loading a state therefore forgets the readback and any copy in flight, so that the first copy the mirror takes is one made after the upload. And waiting for the readback means waiting for one that exists: the first round after a resume dispatches nothing - the ring is still refilling - so the readback is current but empty until a fresh copy lands.

The judge is every learner's: Geno's own task, without the training grace, starts a second apart across the clip, the policy's mean action. Its first line is the servo alone, exactly as a PPO run's is, so the two runs' judgements read against the same baseline. After its first save, each start of the trainer reads its policy file back and has the lab's decider act on every character; the actions must match the learner's own to a few parts in a million - the rounding between summing the goal and the state interleaved and one after the other - or the run fails, rather than leave a policy file the lab would play differently from how it trained.

The judge measures how long a policy keeps the reference when nothing disturbs it. The recovery probe, run at every judgement beside it, measures how the policy comes back when something does. A push is a sudden change of the whole body's velocity - a speed, in a horizontal direction drawn uniformly round the vertical, added to the root's linear velocity, so every body moves with it: an impulse of the character's mass times the speed, through its centre of mass. For each band of push speed, every start of the judge tracks for a second, which sets its level of reward, is pushed once, then watched for three seconds. A push is survived when the failure rule does not fire in the watch, and tracking comes back when the reward's running mean over a quarter of a second returns to nine tenths of its level before the push - with the time it took. A start already lost before its push is not counted; the directions come from the probe's own seed, so every learner is pushed the same way. The probe's lines go to recovery.csv, one per band:

   settle 1 s            push           watch 3 s
   |------------------|     |      |-----------------------------------|
   reward level r                    running mean >= 0.9 r ?   failure rule ?
   band speeds:  1   2   3   4   5 m/s      a push that needs a step ... a fall ... a hard fall

Returns. A push that is not survived is not the end of the question. With returns probed - five seconds by default (return_seconds) - a start that loses the reference is followed on, its reference still running, until it holds the reference again for a few steps in a row (it has returned, and the time from its loss is kept) or the five seconds run out (not returned).
