src/robot_latent_kit.zig

declarationwhat it is
FailureBarrierSuperTrack's failure barrier (zn_mlp.lat_barrier_bwd): a smooth hinge, in the policy's loss at every rolled step, on two of the task's failure measures read from the rolled features - the head's height error and the tilt between the character's up and the reference's - so the pathwise gradient feels the failure rule's cliff before the fall.
TrackingCostSUPERTRACK'S PER-STEP COST - its settings (runTrackingCost): the feature width, the failure barrier and the two columns it reads (the head's height, the up direction), and where the normaliser is - read by the barrier alone, so 0 when the barrier is off.
runTrackingCostSUPERTRACK'S PER-STEP COST of rows states against their goals - the distance from the goal plus the failure barrier (zn_mlp.lat_tracking_cost) - into acts at costs_at [rows], the states and goals packed [rows][features] at states_at and goals_at.
CriticOptionsSuperTrack's critic's settings (LatentCritic): its shape, its discount, and how each update steps - EfficientTDMPC's value heads' settings.
DeviceStatsTHE DEVICE'S NUMBERS FOR THE LOG: statistics the learner's kernels write into a block of the parameter buffer, inside the range the learner reads back every frame - so they reach the host with the weights, at no transfer of their own, a frame or so late on a GPU.
LatentCriticSUPERTRACK'S CRITIC - the tracking cost a character can expect from a state onward, discounted:
PolicyActorWhich policy acts in SuperTrack's rollout and in its fleet: the Gaussian policy SuperTrack is built with, or a flow policy (FlowActor).
FlowSettingsA flow actor's settings, as a learner's options hold them: the velocity network's shape, the sampler's, how the flow learns (FlowActor.Teacher: FlowDPG's step share and anchor, the optimiser's rate and clip), and how long each character's noise remembers itself (zimrrl.ouCorrelation's correlation time).
FlowActorSuperTrack's FLOW ACTOR: a flow policy (kit_mlp.KitFlow) that CORRECTS SuperTrack's policy.
GivenCorrectionsCORRECTIONS GIVEN, NOT SAMPLED: coefficients for every step and row of a rollout, [step][row][synergy] at acts coefficients_at, each step's decoded through the synergies at params synergies_at (synergy_count of them) and added to the policy's raw action, as a flow's correction is (FlowActor).
SkipModelTHE SKIP MODEL - a HEAD of the world model that predicts a whole SPAN of steps at once.
LatentKit—
StartWhere a training window starts: a character, and its first record's replay index.
TrackingScorerTHE TRACKING PLANNER'S SCORER: how good a plan is - H actions from a state - by SuperTrack's own objective.
TrackingPlannerTHE TRACKING PLANNER: MPPI (bmpc_kit.KitMppi, EfficientTDMPC's search on the kit) over SuperTrack's own objective (TrackingScorer).
ResidentThe training data, RESIDENT in the kit's activation buffer: the reference TABLES, uploaded once per clip, and the replay of FEATURES, appended once per simulation step.

src/robot_track_resident.zig

declarationwhat it is
PlanningFlagsWHICH CHARACTERS PLAN, AND WHEN.
PlanningSettingsHow SuperTrack's learner plans for characters in danger (PlanningFlags, robot_latent_kit.TrackingPlanner): whether it does, which characters and when (the flags' settings), and the search for each - its candidates, the plans' horizon in steps, its rounds and elites, how many of the candidates are the flow's own plans, and the temperature, read relative to the elites' own spread.
planningHazardA character's PLANNING HAZARD: how far toward a fall its state is, by the failure barrier's own measures (zn_mlp.barrierMeasuresOf) against the barrier's own margins - the larger of its two fractions,
projectedHazardA hazard PROJECTED ahead along its rise - what the flags read, so a fall in progress is caught early:
Options—
SavedOptionsOptions as a state file holds them: the same fields, with the same names and types, in an extern struct, so that their bytes have one fixed layout on every machine.
StateHeaderEverything a state file holds before its numbers.
FeatureScratchWhat supertrackFeaturesInto works in: the character's state, the reference's state, a model data the reference is posed in (so the fleet's own is never disturbed), and one feature vector before it is normalised.
supertrackFeaturesIntoSuperTrack's two feature vectors for character character of fleet, normalised by normalizer: the STATE - the character's simulated bodies in its root's frame (robot_track.local) - into out_state, and the GOAL - the reference one frame ahead of the character's frame, in the same root's frame - into out_goal.
PolicyPartsWhat a SuperTrack policy file is made of (robot_lab.policyOfSuperTrack), as the learner holds it: the policy's weights as acting uses them (the mirror, packed as LatentKit.packPolicy packs them - the first layer reading the goal then the state as one input, then the two later layers, each its weights then its biases), the network's widths, and the feature normaliser.
HostPolicyTHE POLICY AS THE CPU ACTS WITH IT: the policy's weights as the CPU last saw them, the flow's and the synergies' when the learner has a flow, and the rows inference works in - everything choosing an action needs, and nothing of the GPU's kit.
ActingScratchONE TASK'S SCRATCH FOR ACTING (Resident.computeAction): the host policy's rows - its own, while the mirrored weights are the learner's, read by every task - the states and the probe the features are computed in, and the flow's starting noise.
Resident—

src/kit_mlp.zig

declarationwhat it is
KitBufferWhich of the kit's two working buffers a region lies in: the ACTIVATIONS a forward pass writes (acts), or the GRADIENTS a backward pass writes (dacts).
RowColumnsA run of columns in rows laid out with a stride: row r's columns start at offset + r x row_stride + first_column, in buffer.
copyColumnscolumn_count columns of row_count rows copied from source to destination, on the kit.
KitLayoutThe offsets of everything in the kit's buffers, handed out in order - a counter per buffer, nothing more.
DenseActivationThe activation of a plain network's hidden layers (KitNetwork.initDense, Spec.act).
KitLayerKindWhat a layer is on the kit (this file's head).
KitLayerOne layer's shape, where its parameters are, and its norm's settings.
LayerRegionsWhere one APPLICATION keeps one layer's values (this file's head), each [rows, width] row-major.
ApplicationUseWhat an application is for: a forward and its backward (a network that learns from it), or a forward alone (a network read to act, to plan or to make targets) - which reserves no gradient regions, a third of a layer's floats or more, and refuses a backward.
DropoutWhether an application drops out (KitLayer.dropout): the world model's value heads do while they train; the same heads read as targets, and every network applied to act or to make targets, do not - as on the CPU, where dropout happens only where a generator is handed in.
DropoutGeneratorWhat a dropout mask's generator is the generator OF (Application.writeDropoutMasks): of the whole network, which hands each layer its own split by the layer's index - as zimrnum.Mlp.apply does with the generator it is given - or of the dropout layer itself, used as it is - as zimrnum.Graph.resampleDropout draws each dropout node's mask from its own split of the update's generator.
ParameterGradientsWhat a backward does with the parameters' gradients it computes: write them over what is in grads, or add them to it.
KitNetworkA zimrnum Mlp(f32) on the kit: its layers, each with where its parameters are (this file's head).
SpecWhat a network is: its shape, how it is trained, and how many examples at a time.
KitMlpAn ordinary multilayer perceptron on the kit, with its own pipe and batch (this file's head): one KitNetwork of plain dense layers and one application of it, the batch's inputs and targets beside it, and a training step of mean-squared error and Adam.
ClippedAdamONE CLIPPED ADAM STEP over a contiguous range of parameters - the optimiser step of every network on the kit that learns alone (SuperTrack's critic, a flow actor), on the gradients its backward left in the gradient buffer:
TeacherSharesSHARES OF ONE UPDATE BETWEEN SEVERAL TEACHERS: each teacher's gradient over a network's parameters measured alone, scaled to the share it is given, and summed -
KitFlowTHE FLOW POLICY ON THE KIT - zimrrl.FlowPolicy's sampler and training gradients in the kit's kernels, over the same velocity network (a KitNetwork built from the flow's own Mlp, so the CPU reference's numbers carry over unchanged).

src/robot_bmpc_kit.zig

declarationwhat it is
ColumnPlacementWhat place_columns copies: rows packed rows of count values from acts at source_offset, into columns first_column ..
placeColumnsplacement's copy (place_columns), one thread per value copied.
TwoHotBinsThe bins a two-hot head predicts over (zimrnum.CategoricalScalar): BMPC's 101 on [-10, 10] of the symlog axis.
decodeTwoHotRowsA two-hot head's logits read back as numbers, one per row (twohot_decode): each row's softmax-weighted mean bin position, taken back from the bins' axis - what CategoricalScalar.decodeRows computes on the host - into acts at values_offset.
KitRolloutTHE LATENT ROLLOUT ON THE KIT - zimrrl's LatentRollout, the same arithmetic laid out for the kernels.
KitWorldModelTHE WORLD MODEL ON THE KIT - zimrrl's WorldModelLoss on a KitRollout, the same arithmetic laid out for the kernels.
KitValueTargetsTHE VALUE TARGETS ON THE KIT - zimrrl's LatentValueTargets at BMPC's one-step lookahead, laid out for the kernels, written where the world model's value heads read their targets.
KitPolicyLearnerTHE POLICY LEARNS ON THE KIT - the CPU agent's PolicyLearner.update, laid out for the kernels.
SearchShapeWhat an MPPI search is over (KitMppi), whichever scorer fills it: its states, the candidates of each, the plans' horizon and the action's width; where the candidates' actions are - packed STEP BY STEP, [step][state x candidate][action] (all candidates' first actions, then all their second ones, and so on: the MPPI kernels' layout), written by the search's sampling and read by the scorer - and where their scores are, [state x candidate], higher better.
KitPlanScorerSCORING PLANS ON THE KIT - zimrrl's LatentPlanScorer, laid out for the kernels: every candidate plan of every state rolled through the world model's imagination and given one number, the planner's ranking.
KitPolicyPlansTHE POLICY'S OWN PLANS IN THE SEARCH, ON THE KIT - zimrrl's LatentPolicyPlans: for every state, plans plans the policy itself proposes, rolled through the world model and written as the first candidates of the state's block, where the planner scores them with every other candidate (and never moves them).
planKnotsFitMPPI ON THE KIT - zimrrl's Mppi: each state's Gaussian over plans, the round's candidates drawn from it into the scorer's candidate actions, and the Gaussian refitted to the elites the scores pick (zn_mlp's MPPI section gives the rule).
KitMppi—
KitPlannerONE DECISION ON THE KIT - the CPU actor's act: the policy's own plans, MPPI's rounds around the scorer, the chosen elite's first action, and - while training - its jitter.
KitLearnerONE UPDATE OF EFFICIENTTDMPC ON THE KIT - the CPU agent's Learner.update: a batch of windows sampled from the replay, the world model's update, and (outside pretraining) the policy's, on the kit's pieces - KitRollout, KitWorldModel, KitValueTargets, KitPolicyLearner - over networks its caller placed (and shares with the planner).
placeAgentNetworksEvery network of an agent placed in layout in the world model's order - the encoder, every dynamics head, the reward head, every value head, every target value head - then the policy (the order KitWorldModel's clip and KitLearner assume).
writeAgentParamsEvery network's numbers written into params, the layout's parameter block, where placeAgentNetworks placed it.
KitTrainerEFFICIENTTDMPC TRAINED ON THE KIT - the CPU agent's Trainer, frame for frame: the kit's planner acts for every environment, the host steps the environments and stores every step in the replay with the planner's target, and the kit's learner makes the schedule's updates.

src/robot_maximal.zig

declarationwhat it is
densityMJCF's default density, which its inertia-from-geoms uses.
no_partThe part index of a robot body no part stands for: the world body.
Variant—
TwistHingeWhich of a body's hinges becomes a swing-twist joint's TWIST: the one limit it keeps exactly.
Options—
JointOne joint between two parts, and the pivot it holds together in each part's COM-centred frame, captured when it was built.
DriveA joint drive: a spring toward a target, stated as a FREQUENCY.
stableSpringAccelThe acceleration a critically damped (for damping 1) spring of frequency Hz asks of one joint over a step of dt, evaluated IMPLICITLY - at the end of the step.
stableSpringAccelTowardThe same spring, damped toward a MOVING target's velocity instead of zero - velocity feedforward.
floatingBaseTorquesJoint torques that give a FLOATING-base model the joint accelerations accel asks for (root entries ignored), with the root free to respond - floating-base inverse dynamics.
FrameA robot body frame in the world: origin and rotation.
Ragdoll—
buildRebuild m in world as rigid bodies and joints, posed as d holds (d current).
limpReducedThe plan's "limp" baseline on the REDUCED side: no joint stiffness, damping or armature and no tendon springs, because the maximal side has none of them.
worstJointErrorDegWorst joint rotation error, in degrees: for each joint the angle between the child's rotation relative to its parent now and in the target.

src/gpu/zn_mlp.zig

declarationwhat it is
config—
ActWhat a layer's output goes through.
MppiTemperatureWhether a loss kernel counts every row, or only the rows a mask marks (row_mask): a replay window that has run past its episode's end still rolls forward, but its rows count for nothing in the loss from then on.
RowMask—
TwoHotAxisHow the two-hot kernels place a value on their bins' axis (zimrnum.CategoricalScalar.Axis): its symlog (DreamerV3, TD-MPC2, BMPC), or the value itself.
ParamsEverything a dispatch needs, written by the host before it.
acts_lenThe activation buffer is the one that grows: eight times the others.
dacts_lenThe activation gradients' buffer, sized on its own: a learner's backward keeps a gradient for every activation of every application it learns from - EfficientTDMPC's rollout over a whole batch of windows, every head at every step - so it grows with the batch, where the parameters and their gradients and moments grow only with the networks (config.max each).
Buffers—
g—
dense_fwdy[r, o] = act(b[o] + sum_i x[r, i] W[i, o]); one thread per (r, o).
act_bwddy[r, o] *= act'(y[r, o]), in place: the gradient at the pre-activation.
dense_bwd_xdx[r, i] = sum_o dz[r, o] W[i, o]; one thread per (r, i).
dense_bwd_wgW[i, o] = sum_r x[r, i] dz[r, o], then gb[o] = sum_r dz[r, o]: one thread per weight.
mse_bwdThe gradient of a mean squared error, one thread per value: for the loss mean over n values of (y - t)^2, each value's gradient is 2 (y - t) / n - then times loss_weight, its term's weight in a weighted loss (1 for the error alone).
mse_valueloss[0] = mean (y - t)^2, one thread: for the readback, not for training.
ppo_mean_gradd loss / d mean[r, k]: one thread per (row, action dimension), into dacts[dy_off].
ppo_logstd_gradd loss / d log_std[k]: one thread per action dimension, summed over the rows, into grads.
adamAdam over count elements from w_off, with the host's bias corrections.
grad_square_partialsThe sum of squares of one chunk of the gradients, ONE THREAD PER CHUNK: count gradients from grads at w_off, in chunks of stride - chunk id covers [id x stride, (id + 1) x stride), the last one what is left - each chunk's compensated sum into acts at y_off + id.
clip_factorThe global norm and the clip factor, ONE THREAD: the square root of the rows partial sums at acts x_off (grad_square_partials), summed with compensation, into acts z_off; the factor - clip / norm past the limit, exactly 1 within it - into acts z_off + 1.
share_factorA TEACHER'S SHARE, ONE THREAD: the length of its gradient - the square root of the rows partial sums at acts x_off (grad_square_partials), summed with compensation - into acts z_off, and the factor that scales it to length loss_weight, its share, into acts z_off + 1: share / length, or 0 for a gradient of no length (a teacher that taught nothing adds nothing) - kit_mlp.TeacherShares.
add_scaled_gradientsA TEACHER'S GRADIENT, SCALED, INTO THE SUM - ONE THREAD PER PARAMETER: count gradients from grads w_off times the factor at acts x_off (share_factor), into acts y_off - added to what is there (col 1), or written over it for the first teacher (col 0).
gradients_from_sumTHE SUMMED GRADIENTS BACK WHERE THE OPTIMISER READS THEM - ONE THREAD PER PARAMETER: count numbers from acts y_off into grads w_off.
adam_clippedAdam on clipped gradients, ONE THREAD PER PARAMETER: count parameters from w_off, each gradient times the clip factor at acts x_off (clip_factor) - one multiplication, as zimrnum's clip scales each gradient in place before its Adam reads it - then adam's step.
norm_fwdA normed layer's norm, ONE THREAD PER ROW: rows rows of out_dim pre-activations p at x_off, normalised by the row's own statistics (zm.layerNormRowStatistics, epsilon norm_epsilon), each then times its gain plus its norm bias - from params at w_off, the gains [out_dim] then the norm biases [out_dim].
mish_fwdMish on rows x out_dim values, ONE THREAD PER VALUE: y = Mish(s) from x_off into y_off (zm.mish).
simnorm_fwdSimNorm on rows x out_dim values, ONE THREAD PER GROUP: each row's values in consecutive groups of simnorm_group, each group softmaxed (zm.softmaxGroupStatistics, zm.softmaxGroupValue) - from x_off into y_off.
mish_bwdMish's backward, ONE THREAD PER VALUE: ds = dy * Mish'(s) (zm.mishSlope), s from acts at x_off (mish_fwd's input), dy from dacts at dy_off, ds into dacts at dx_off (which may be dy_off: each value reads its own).
simnorm_bwdSimNorm's backward, ONE THREAD PER GROUP: each input's gradient its probability times how far its arriving gradient is from the group's probability-weighted sum (zm.softmaxGroupGradientDot, zm.softmaxGroupInputGradient).
norm_params_bwdA normed layer's gain and norm bias gradients, ONE THREAD PER PARAMETER: thread c < out_dim sums ds * n down column c (the gain's gradient), thread out_dim + c sums ds down it (the norm bias's) - compensated, as zimrnum's reductions are.
norm_bwdA normed layer's norm, backward, ONE THREAD PER ROW: the gradient at the pre-activations p from the gradient ds at s (dacts at dy_off), through the gain (params at w_off) and the norm - the row's couplings (zm.layerNormGradientCouplings) over dn = ds * gain and the forward's normalised row n (acts at z_off), each input's gradient by zm.layerNormInputGradient with the row's inverse spread (acts at l_off).
twohot_fwdThe two-hot cross-entropy of each row, ONE THREAD PER ROW: out_dim logits from acts at x_off, the row's target value from acts at t_off (one a row), the row's loss into acts at y_off (one a row).
twohot_bwdThe two-hot cross-entropy's gradient at the logits, ONE THREAD PER ROW: (target mass x softmax_j - target_j) / twohot_divisor x loss_weight for each of the row's out_dim logits (acts at x_off), the targets from acts at t_off, into dacts at dy_off.
twohot_decodeA two-hot head's prediction, ONE THREAD PER ROW: the softmax's probability-weighted mean bin position (zm.binPosition), taken back from the axis - zimrnum's CategoricalScalar.decode, term for term.
twohot_value_bwdThe SLOPE of a two-hot head's decoded value in its logits, ONE THREAD PER ROW - twohot_decode run backward, for a loss that uses the decoded value itself (SuperTrack's value tail).
ensemble_tail_weightsEach head's weight per row in a PESSIMISTIC ensemble cost, ONE THREAD PER ROW: the cost an ensemble of H heads reports is their mean plus plan_pessimism (beta) of their spread -
policy_divergenceThe policy's divergence from the planner at each row, ONE THREAD PER ROW: policy_distill_bwd's first half, for the running scale - which must move with this batch's divergences before the gradients divide by it (torch BMPC's order), and divergences do not depend on the scale.
policy_distill_bwdThe policy's distillation loss, backward, ONE THREAD PER ROW (this section's head): for rows rows of out_dim action dimensions - reads acts x_off the policy network's raw outputs [rows, 2 x dims]: raw centres, then raw spreads t_off the planner's means [rows, dims]; u_off the logs of its spreads [rows, dims] v_off each row's weight [rows]; e_off the scale's reciprocal (one value) writes dacts dy_off the gradient at the raw outputs [rows, 2 x dims] acts y_off each row's divergence, KL / dims [rows]; z_off each row's entropy [rows] The spread's bounds and the entropy's coefficient are distill_log_std_low, _high, distill_entropy_coefficient.
running_scale_updateBMPC's running scale, moved by one batch, ONE THREAD (zimrnum.RunningScale.update): the count values at acts x_off - the first step's divergences, from policy_divergence - copied into acts z_off and sorted there, their 5th and 95th percentiles (zm.quantileOfSorted, the host's own interpolation), and the scale at acts v_off - which persists from update to update, 1 to start - moved a fraction tau toward their spread (zm.runningScaleStep).
policy_drawThe policy's draw at each row, ONE THREAD PER ROW (zm.tanhMeanGaussianDraw, the host's own): from the policy network's raw outputs at acts x_off [rows, 2 x dims] through the head (policyHead, its bounds distill_log_std_low and _high) and the standard normal noise at acts u_off [rows, dims], each action written into the action columns of the wide rows at acts y_off - rows stride apart, from column col - where the reward head and the dynamics heads read it beside its latent.
value_target_combineEach stored step's value target, ONE THREAD PER ROW, in zimrrl.LatentValueTargets.compute's order of arithmetic: for each of target_dynamics_heads heads in turn, its own target - the reward, then gamma over the value-head count times each of target_value_heads target values, added in order - and the heads' targets summed in order and scaled once by 1 / heads (a single head's target taken as it is).
broadcast_rowsEach of rows packed source rows of count values (acts at x_off) copied to row_copies consecutive destination rows, into columns col ..
copy_row_blocksRows carried from a packed layout of plan_policy_plans rows per state into each state's block of plan_candidates candidate rows, ONE THREAD PER VALUE: source row r = state x plans + plan, read at acts x_off + r x stride + col (count values - the action columns of the policy plans' wide rows), written packed at acts y_off + (state x candidates + plan) x count - the step's block of the scorer's candidate actions, where the policy's plans are the first rows of each state's block.
plan_score_combineEvery candidate's score and variance, ONE THREAD PER CANDIDATE ROW (this section's head): rows candidate rows, reads acts x_off the decoded rewards, [dynamics head][step][rows] acts v_off the decoded values, [dynamics head][depth][value head][rows] (the depths with weight) acts u_off the objective's weights: plan_horizon reward weights, then as many value weights writes acts y_off each candidate's score: the dynamics heads' mean, less plan_pessimism standard deviations acts z_off each candidate's variance of that mean: the estimates' variance over their count
mppi_sampleThe round's candidates drawn from each state's Gaussian, ONE THREAD PER (state, candidate, step, dimension): for rows states of plan_candidates candidates, each candidate from plan_policy_plans on (the policy's own rows are left alone) gets mean + spread x noise, clamped to [-1, 1] - reads acts t_off the means, u_off the spreads, [states][horizon][action] each; acts v_off the noise, [states][candidates][horizon][action] writes acts y_off the candidates' actions, [horizon][states x candidates][action] (the scorer's layout)
mppi_elitesEach state's elites and their weights, ONE THREAD PER STATE: of its plan_candidates scores at acts x_off (made rankable, zm.rankableScore), the best mppi_elites, best first, in the host's order - the host sorts ascending and stably and reads from the end, so among equal scores the higher candidate comes first.
mppi_refitEach state's Gaussian refitted to its elites, ONE THREAD PER (state, step, dimension): the elites' weighted mean, then - in a second pass, as the host - their weighted variance about it, and its square root clamped to [mppi_min_spread, mppi_max_spread] - reads acts x_off the candidates' actions, [horizon][states x candidates][action]; acts y_off the elites' candidate numbers, z_off their weights, [states][elites] each writes acts t_off the means, u_off the spreads, [states][horizon][action] each
mppi_beginThe warm start, ONE THREAD PER (state, action dimension) walking the plan's steps in order: for rows states, where the state's flag at acts x_off is 1 the plan moves forward by mppi_warm_shift steps - the steps since it was decided, 1 for a planner that decides every step - each step's mean becoming that of the step S later, the last S steps' 0; where the flag is 0 every step's mean is 0.
mppi_chooseThe choice, ONE THREAD PER STATE (Mppi.choose with draw_elite, BMPC's): one elite drawn by the refit's weights - the uniform draw at acts v_off + state against the weights' running sum, in rank order, the first rank whose sum exceeds it (the last rank if rounding leaves none) - and its FIRST action, the decision's target, with the first step's spread beside it - reads acts x_off the candidates' actions, [horizon][states x candidates][action] (step 0's block); acts y_off the elites' candidate numbers, z_off their weights, [states][elites] each; acts u_off the spreads, [states][horizon][action] writes acts t_off the targets and t_off + states x action the first spreads, [states][action] each; acts e_off + state: the chosen candidate's number
mppi_exploreThe jitter while training, ONE THREAD PER (state, action dimension) (Mppi.explore): the target plus its spread times a standard normal draw, clamped to [-1, 1] - the targets at acts t_off and the first spreads after them (mppi_choose's layout), the noise at acts v_off, [states][action]; the actions acted on to acts y_off.
squash_fwdu = mean + std eps, a = tanh(u): u kept at acts[u_off], the action written into a strided block (acts[z_off + r stride + col + k]).
squash_logplog pi per row: sum over dimensions of -eps^2/2 - log std - log(2 pi)/2 - log(1 - tanh(u)^2).
sac_targety = r + discount (min(q1', q2') - alpha log pi'): q1' at acts[y_off], q2' at acts[z_off], log pi' at acts[l_off], rewards then DISCOUNTS at acts[x_off] - the replay row's last column, gamma (1 - done) for a one-step row, gamma^k for an n-step one; y to acts[t_off].
min_routeThe actor loss's -mean(min(q1, q2)) gradient, routed WHOLE to the smaller critic (ties go to the first, as zimrnum's graph min): into dacts[dy_off] for q1 and dacts[dx_off] for q2.
squash_bwddL/du for the actor loss mean(alpha log pi - min q): the critics' gradient at their action input (both blocks, dacts[dx_off] and dacts[e_off], strided; one of each row's is zero) through tanh, plus alpha's pull through the squash correction (d/du of -log(1 - tanh^2) is 2 tanh).
squash_logstd_gradThe raw log-std's gradient: sum over rows of dL/du std eps, less alpha (the -log std in log pi, averaged), through the tanh bound.
alpha_gradLog alpha's gradient, -alpha (mean log pi + target entropy): zrl.Temperature.gradient.
polyakA target network's slow follow over count params - each target value moved tau of the way to its online twin (zm.polyakFollow: the increment form, the endpoints exact - zimrnum's own, so the host and the kit follow to the same bits).
cp_wm_input[cart rate, pole angle, pole rate] of the state at acts[x_off] and the force at acts[u_off] into the world model's input rows at acts[z_off].
cp_wm_input_bwdThe world-model input's gradient (dacts[dx_off], rows x 4) back to the state: ADDED into the state gradient at dacts[dy_off] (columns 1-3); the force's share to dacts[e_off].
cp_forceThe policy's force: tanh(o + sigma eps), o at acts[y_off], eps at acts[x_off], into acts[u_off].
cp_force_bwdd loss / d o: the force's gradient (dacts[e_off]) through tanh, plus the action penalty's 2 w_action o / rows.
cp_stepOne integration step: the state at acts[x_off], the world model's output at acts[y_off] (rows x 2), the next state to acts[z_off].
cp_step_bwdcp_step's adjoint: the next state's gradient (dacts[dy_off]) to the state's (dacts[e_off], OVERWRITTEN - this starts the step's state gradient) and the world model output's (dacts[dx_off], rows x 2).
cp_track_bwdThe tracking loss's gradient at a state (acts[x_off], rows x 4) against a target (acts[t_off]): 2 w_c (s - t) / rows, into dacts[dy_off] - ADDED when accumulate.
place_columnsA packed block written into columns of a wider, strided one (this section's head): rows x count values from acts at x_off into acts at y_off, rows stride apart, columns col ..
take_columnsColumns of a wide gradient block copied out into a packed one (the joins' head): rows x count values from dacts at dx_off (rows stride apart, columns col ..
mask_valuesDropout in a layer, forward, ONE THREAD PER VALUE: count values in acts at x_off multiplied in place by the mask at acts z_off - each mask value 1 / keep for a kept unit, 0 for a dropped one (inverted dropout, the mask drawn once per update: zimrnum.fillDropoutMask).
mask_gradientsDropout in a layer, backward, ONE THREAD PER VALUE: count gradients in dacts at dy_off multiplied in place by the forward's mask at acts z_off - a dropped unit passes no gradient back, a kept one passes it scaled as its value was.
add_blockdacts[dy_off + i] += dacts[dx_off + i] over count: a gradient arriving by a second path.
lat_advanceThe next state, in two places at once: z_{k+1} = z_k + change, written into the next block's z columns (strided, so the next step's first layer reads it) AND into a contiguous block (the loss kernels read contiguous rows).
lat_scale_columnsA GRADIENT BLOCK'S COLUMNS SCALED, ONE THREAD PER VALUE: rows rows of count columns from dacts x_off into dacts y_off (the same place for in place), each column times its own factor from acts u_off + column.
lat_takeThe backward join: the gradient that reached a block's z columns (strided, at dx_off) added into the state's contiguous gradient (at dy_off) - the path by which the loss at later steps reaches earlier states THROUGH the network, beside the residual path add_block carries.
latRecordWidthFloats in one record of the feature ring: a character's raw (unnormalised) features, the action it took on that step, and one more for which reference-table row it was aiming at.
latRecordTableRowWhere a record's reference-table row sits: the last column, kept as a float like everything else in the buffer and rounded back to an integer when read.
latTableWidthFloats in one row of the reference tables: a frame's features, then the servo targets the fleet would aim at for it - everything a rollout needs about a reference frame, so a window can be built without the clips being on the device at all.
latRecordActionWhere a record's action begins.
lat_gatherA batch of training windows, assembled on the GPU from what is resident there: the feature ring (a record per character per step: raw features, action, table row), the reference tables (a row per clip frame: raw goal features, encoded targets) and the normaliser (means, then spreads).
latNoise—
latUniformA hashed UNIFORM number in [0, 1) for row under seed: the hash's top 24 bits, as a fraction - every value a multiple of 2^-24, each equally likely.
latStepSeedA different seed for every step of the rollout, from one seed per training step.
lat_actThe policy's action into its row: lat_scale * raw into the wide row's action columns, so the world model's next step reads the action the policy just chose.
lat_act_bwdThe action's gradient back to the policy's raw output: d raw = lat_scale * d action + lat_penalty * raw.
BarrierMeasuresThe failure barrier's two measures for one row: the head's height error (the character's height minus the reference's, in metres), and the dot product and squared lengths of the character's and the reference's up directions, from which their cosine - and so the tilt - and its gradient follow.
barrierMeasuresOfThe barrier's measures for one row of normalised features - the state and its goal, the normaliser's means and spreads - each read through a row accessor (zm.requireRowAccess): the kernels read the buffers (ActsRow), the host reads slices.
barrierHingesThe barrier's VALUE before its weight: the head's hinge on |height error| plus the tilt's hinge on 1 - cos(up, up_ref) (zm.smoothHinge, each with its margin and width).
lat_barrier_bwdThe failure barrier's gradient, ONE THREAD PER ROW, ADDED to a rolled step's state gradient (this section's head): for rows rows of out_dim features - reads acts y_off the rolled features Z, t_off the goal G (the reference's features), both normalised, [rows, features]; acts u_off the normaliser's means, then its spreads, out_dim each adds into dacts dy_off the gradient of barrier_weight / rows x (the head's hinge + the tilt's hinge) The columns, the weight, the margins and the widths are the barrier_ fields.
boundedCostA per-step cost BOUNDED far from the reference: cap x tanh(cost / cap).
lat_tracking_costSuperTrack's per-step TRACKING COST of a state, ONE THREAD PER ROW - what its policy's loss charges a rolled step (mse_bwd and lat_barrier_bwd are this cost's gradient, averaged over the rows), and what its critic sums into the future:
flow_time_featuresThe flow time as the velocity network reads it, ONE THREAD PER (row, sine-cosine pair): for pair p the frequency f = 2^p and the pair [sin(pi f t), cos(pi f t)] - half a cycle over [0, 1] at the lowest frequency, so no two times look alike.
flow_euler_stepOne EULER STEP of the flow, ONE THREAD PER (row, action dimension): x_(k+1) = x_k + flow_step x v(x_k).
flow_path_pointsThe STRAIGHT PATH for training, ONE THREAD PER (row, action dimension): each row's point x_t = (1 - t) x_0 + t a and the path's velocity there, a - x_0.
hashed_noiseHASHED NORMAL NOISE into columns of strided rows, ONE THREAD PER (row, column): lat_sigma times the hashed standard normal of (row, column) under the seed lat_seed (latNoise), into acts at y_off + row x stride + col + column, count columns.
copy_columnsA run of columns copied from one strided row layout to another, ONE THREAD PER VALUE: count columns of each of rows rows, read at acts x_off + row x stride + col + column, written at acts y_off + row x destination_stride + destination_column + column.
copy_columns_from_gradientscopy_columns from the GRADIENT buffer: the same run of columns read from dacts, written into acts - a gradient a backward left (an action's, for one) handed on as data to a step that reads it from acts (FlowDPG's cost gradient).
hashed_uniformsHASHED UNIFORM NUMBERS, ONE THREAD PER ROW: each row's number drawn uniformly from [0, 1) (latUniform under lat_seed), into acts at y_off + row.
flow_dpg_bwdFLOWDPG'S GRADIENT at the velocity, ONE THREAD PER ROW.
plan_gatherTHE TRACKING PLANNER'S GATHER, ONE THREAD PER NUMBER WRITTEN over rows x (lat_steps + 1) x width: a planner kit's rows - [state][candidate], plan_candidates rows per state - filled from each state's start and the reference table, in lat_gather's conventions, so a planned rollout sees what a training window would: * GOAL columns (the first lat_lead), step k >= 1: the reference where step k - 1 is going - table row (start + k), normalised - into wide row k - 1's goal columns and goal block G_k: the flow's condition at step k - 1, and the cost's goal for the state that step produces * STATE columns, step 0: the state's start, already normalised * REFERENCE columns, step k < lat_steps: table row (start + k)'s encoded targets - a table row is [goal | encoded targets] and the world model's slice [state | reference | action], so the reference sits at the same offset in both * ACTION columns: left alone - the search's and the flow's to write The table rows run on from the state's start row and hold at its clip's last row, as the training records do.
flow_draw_lossesEACH EXAMPLE'S FLOW MATCHING LOSS, AVERAGED OVER ITS DRAWS, ONE THREAD PER EXAMPLE - FPO's stand-in for an action's negative log-likelihood (zimrrl.FlowPolicy.drawLosses, whose arithmetic this is).
fpo_advantagesTEACHER 3'S ADVANTAGE, ONE THREAD PER EXAMPLE: how a real step turned out against what the critic expected,
stat_copyONE NUMBER COPIED: the activation at acts x_off into params stat_off - a value another kernel already worked out, such as a clipped optimiser's gradient length, kept for the log.
stat_root_mean_squareTHE ROOT MEAN SQUARE of rows gradients at dacts x_off - how large a gradient is, whatever its sign - into params stat_off.
stat_mean_square_differenceTHE MEAN SQUARED DIFFERENCE of rows activations at acts x_off and at acts t_off - a regression's loss per number, as flow matching's is between the velocity given and the path's - into params stat_off.
stat_mean_and_deviationTHE MEAN AND THE SAMPLE DEVIATION of rows activations at acts x_off - the deviation divided by rows - 1, as zimrrl.normalizeAdvantages takes it; 0 for fewer than two - into params stat_off and stat_off + 1.
lat_skip_gatherTHE SKIP HEAD'S INPUTS (SkipModel), ONE THREAD PER VALUE: for each of count jumps of col steps through a window of the latent kit's rollout, and each of its rows rows, the row the head reads -
lat_skip_targetsTHE SKIP HEAD'S TARGETS (SkipModel), ONE THREAD PER VALUE: each jump's change over its col steps, from the state it starts at to the RECORDED state after its last step - for count jumps of rows rows of in_dim features.
plan_gain_statsTHE PLANNER'S GAIN over its proposals, ONE THREAD: for rows states of plan_candidates candidates, the first plan_policy_plans of each the actor's own proposals (the flow's plans) and the rest drawn by the search - the scores at acts x_off [states x candidates], each state's chosen candidate at acts e_off + state (a number held in a float) - into params stat_off the chosen plan's score less the best proposal's, averaged over the states, and into stat_off + 1 the share of states whose chosen plan is one the search drew.
critic_value_statsTHE CRITIC'S HEADS on a batch: count heads' decoded values at acts x_off, [head][row] for rows rows, and the rows' targets at acts t_off - into params stat_off the heads' mean value, stat_off + 1 their mean SPREAD (each row's standard deviation across the heads, averaged over the rows: the disagreement a pessimistic critic adds to its value), and stat_off + 2 the heads' error against the targets as a root mean square, in the cost's own units.
stat_barrierTHE FAILURE BARRIER'S HINGES over a rollout: count steps of rows rows, each step's rolled states at acts y_off and goals at t_off advancing one block (rows x out_dim) a step, the normaliser at u_off - each row's head and tilt hinges as the tracking cost charges them (barrierMeasures, barrierHinges, the barrier_ fields), their mean into params stat_off, unweighted: 0 while every imagined state keeps well inside the failure rule, larger the more and the deeper the rollouts press against it.
fpo_ratio_statsFPO'S RATIOS over rows examples - each exp(L_old - L_new), from the old losses at acts x_off and the new at u_off - their mean into params stat_off, and into stat_off + 1 the share of examples the clip holds: those whose clipped term is the smaller, decided with the advantages at v_off and the clip exactly as fpo_velocity_gradient decides it.
fpo_normalize_advantagesA BATCH'S ADVANTAGES NORMALISED, ONE THREAD FOR THE WHOLE BATCH - zero mean, unit deviation, in zimrrl.normalizeAdvantages' arithmetic and order: the mean, the SAMPLE deviation (divided by rows - 1), and each advantage minus the mean over the deviation plus advantage_epsilon - so a batch of equal advantages, legitimate if uninformative, gives zeros rather than a division by zero.
fpo_velocity_gradientFPO'S GRADIENT ON EACH DRAW'S VELOCITY, ONE THREAD PER (row, action number).
synergy_decode_addA flow's correction DECODED AND ADDED, ONE THREAD PER (row, action): raw[row][a] += sum over j of c[row][j] B[j][a].
synergy_project_gradientA raw action's gradient PROJECTED ONTO THE SYNERGIES, ONE THREAD PER (row, synergy): g_c[row][j] = sum over a of B[j][a] g[row][a] - the gradient with respect to the flow's coefficients.
plan_mailboxTHE TRACKING PLANNER'S MAILBOX, ONE THREAD PER (state, step, action dimension): each state's chosen plan - the whole plan of the candidate its decision chose (mppi_choose's choice at acts e_off), not the search's mean, which averages elites and so, between two ways back, would take neither - copied out of the candidates' actions (acts x_off, [step][states x plan_candidates][action]) into the PARAMETER buffer at y_off + 1, [state][step] [action].
st_policy_fwdThe policy's window forward, one thread per row: starts at acts[z_off], noise per step at acts[y_off + step rows + r].
st_world_fwdThe world model's window forward, one thread per row: the real start at acts[z_off], the real forces per step at acts[y_off + step rows + r].
st_policy_bwdThe policy's window backward, one thread per row, in reverse: the tracking gradient (target upright, zeros), the step's adjoint, back through the world model to its input (no world-model gradients), the force, the policy - its weight gradients into this row's slice.
st_world_bwdThe world model's window backward, one thread per row, in reverse: the gradient against the real next states (acts[t_off + (step rows + r) 4]), the step's adjoint, the world model's backward WITH its weight gradients into this row's slice.
st_reducegrads[w_off + j] = sum over rows of the per-row gradients (dacts[dx_off + r count + j]).
kernels—
